title.zh: 卷422 列傳二百九 王茂荫 宋晋 袁希祖 文瑞 毓禄 徐继畬 王發桂 廉兆纶 雷以𫍯 陶梁 吴存义 殷兆镛
title.en: Volume 422 Biographies 209: Wang Maoyin, Song Jin, Yuan Xizu, Wen Rui, Yu Lu, Xu Jishe, Wang Fagui, Lian Zhaolun, Lei Yixian, Tao Liang, Wu Cunyi, Yin Zhaoyong
title.raw: 卷422 列傳二百九 王茂荫 宋晋 袁希祖 文瑞 毓禄 徐继畬 王發桂 廉兆纶 雷以𫍯 陶梁 吴存义 殷兆镛

sentences.zh: =王茂廕=王茂廕，字椿年，安徽歙縣人。

translations.literal: Wang Maoyin, courtesy name Chunnian, was a native of She County in Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Maoyin, whose courtesy name was Chunnian, came from She County in Anhui Province.

sentences.zh: 道光十二年進士，授戶部主事，升員外郎。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of the Daoguang reign he passed the jinshi examination, was appointed a principal clerk in the Ministry of Revenue, and was promoted to assistant department director.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in 1832, was appointed a principal clerk in the Ministry of Revenue, and later rose to assistant department director.

sentences.zh: 咸豐元年，遷御史。

translations.literal: In the first year of the Xianfeng reign he was transferred to censor.
translations.idiomatic: In 1851 he was transferred to the post of censor.

sentences.zh: 疏請振獎人才，鄉會試務覈實，殿試、朝考重文義，造就宗室、八旗人才，以有裨實用為貴。

translations.literal: He memorialized requesting encouragement and reward for talent, that the provincial and metropolitan examinations should stress verification of substance, that the palace examination and court examination should emphasize literary meaning, and that talent among the imperial clan and the Eight Banners should be cultivated, valuing what was truly useful in practice.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial urging the court to reward talent, to make provincial and metropolitan examinations test real ability, to weigh substance in the palace and court examinations, and to train useful men among the imperial clan and the Eight Banners rather than mere book learning.

sentences.zh: 戶部議開捐納舉人、生員例，茂廕疏爭，且言：「籌餉之法，不徒在開源，而在於善用。

translations.literal: When the Ministry of Revenue deliberated opening a precedent for purchasing juren and sheng-yuan degrees by contribution, Maoyin memorialized in opposition, saying: 'The method of raising funds lies not merely in opening new sources, but in making good use of them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Ministry of Revenue proposed selling juren and licentiate degrees for cash, Maoyin protested in a memorial, arguing that raising revenue depended not only on finding new income but on spending it wisely.

sentences.zh: 委諸盜賊之手，靡諸老弱之兵，銷諸不肖之員弁，雖日言推廣捐輸，何濟？」

translations.literal: If entrusted to the hands of bandits, squandered on old and weak soldiers, and consumed by unworthy officers, though one daily speaks of extending contributions, what good will it do?"
translations.idiomatic: If funds are handed to bandits, wasted on decrepit troops, or swallowed by incompetent officers, no amount of talk about expanding donations will help."

sentences.zh: 又極論：「銀票虧商，銀號虧國。

translations.literal: He also argued at length: "Bank drafts harm merchants; private banks harm the state.
translations.idiomatic: He went on to argue forcefully that bank drafts injured merchants while private banking houses injured the state.

sentences.zh: 經國謀猷，下同商賈，體至褻而利實至微。

translations.literal: Statecraft and national planning were brought down to the level of merchants; the form was utterly debased while the actual profit was extremely slight.
translations.idiomatic: To place national policy on the same footing as shopkeepers debased the state while yielding almost no real benefit.

sentences.zh: 初時虧不能見，及虧折已甚，雖重治其罪，亦復奚補！」

translations.literal: At first the losses could not be seen; when the losses had already become severe, even if one punished the crime severely, what further remedy was there?"
translations.idiomatic: Losses are invisible at first; by the time they are grave, even harsh punishment cannot repair the damage."

sentences.zh: 其言皆驗。

translations.literal: All his words were later verified.
translations.idiomatic: Events proved him right on every count.

sentences.zh: 二年，粵匪自長沙趨岳州，茂廕疏言：「安徽防務，以宿松為要衝，小孤山為鎖鑰。

translations.literal: In the second year, as the Cantonese rebels moved from Changsha toward Yuezhou, Maoyin memorialized: "For Anhui's defenses, Susong is the vital pass and Little Gushan the strategic lock.
translations.idiomatic: In 1852, as the Taiping forces advanced from Changsha toward Yuezhou, Maoyin wrote that Susong was the critical point in Anhui's defenses and Little Gushan the key to holding them.

sentences.zh: 設險非難，得人為難。

translations.literal: Establishing defenses is not difficult; finding the right men is difficult.
translations.idiomatic: It is easy to fortify positions; the hard part is finding men who can hold them.

sentences.zh: 請起前署廣西巡撫週天爵幫辦防堵，扼要駐守陸路，令府縣勸諭紳民團練守助，用明金聲禦流賊保鄉里之法，最為簡易。」

translations.literal: He requested that the former acting governor of Guangxi, Zhou Tianjue, be recalled to assist in blocking defenses, to hold the vital points along the land route, and that prefectures and districts be ordered to urge gentry and people to organize militia for defense and support, using the Ming method by which Jin Sheng defended against roving bandits to protect the countryside—the simplest approach."
translations.idiomatic: He asked that Zhou Tianjue, former acting governor of Guangxi, be brought back to organize the blockade, garrison the strategic land routes, and have local officials rally gentry militia along the lines of Jin Sheng's Ming-dynasty defense of home districts against roving rebels—the simplest and most effective method."

sentences.zh: 武昌既陷，茂廕又疏言：「賊勢猖獗，宜急收人心，籌儲積，講訓練，求人才。」

translations.literal: After Wuchang had fallen, Maoyin again memorialized: "The rebels are rampant; one should urgently win hearts, lay up stores, conduct training, and seek talent."
translations.idiomatic: After Wuchang fell, he urged the court to rally popular support, build up reserves, drill troops, and recruit capable men while the rebellion still raged."

sentences.zh: 三年，戶部奏試行鈔法，上命左都御史花沙納與茂廕會議，奏行簡要章程，並繪鈔式以進。

translations.literal: In the third year the Ministry of Revenue memorialized to trial paper currency; the emperor ordered the left censor-in-chief Hua Shana and Maoyin to confer, and they memorialized a concise set of regulations and submitted drawings of the note design.
translations.idiomatic: In 1853 the Ministry of Revenue proposed a trial of paper money. The emperor ordered Hua Shana, left censor-in-chief, and Maoyin to draft regulations together; they submitted simplified rules and sample designs for the notes.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「皖北蒙、亳，捻匪蜂起，萬一粵賊勾結，更為心腹巨患。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "In northern Anhui at Mengcheng and Bozhou, Nian bandits are swarming; should they join with the Cantonese rebels, the danger to the heartland would be still greater.
translations.idiomatic: He warned that Nian rebels were rising in Mengcheng and Bozhou in northern Anhui, and that an alliance with the Taiping forces would pose a grave threat to the interior.

sentences.zh: 夫欲平盜賊，尤在守令得人。

translations.literal: If one wishes to pacify bandits, it depends above all on having the right prefects and magistrates.
translations.idiomatic: Suppressing banditry depends above all on appointing capable prefects and magistrates.

sentences.zh: 廬、鳳、潁諸郡，守令貪鄙者，實繁有徒。

translations.literal: In the prefectures of Luzhou, Fengyang, and Yingzhou, greedy and base prefects and magistrates are indeed numerous.
translations.idiomatic: In Luzhou, Fengyang, Yingzhou, and neighboring districts, corrupt and incompetent local officials were legion.

sentences.zh: 請嚴飭大吏從嚴劾汰，以治賊之源。」

translations.literal: He requested that high officials be strictly ordered to impeach and remove them severely, so as to treat the root of banditry."
translations.idiomatic: He asked that provincial authorities be ordered to investigate and dismiss them rigorously, attacking the root cause of the disorder."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「兩湖、江、皖處處言防，而處處不守。

translations.literal: He also said: "In the two Hu provinces, Jiangsu, and Anhui, everywhere they speak of defense, yet everywhere they do not hold.
translations.idiomatic: He added that Hunan, Hubei, Jiangsu, and Anhui all talked of defense but failed to hold their ground anywhere.

sentences.zh: 請嚴飭各督撫專主剿辦，一處賊平，則他處之賊不敢復起；

translations.literal: He requested that each governor-general and governor be strictly ordered to concentrate on suppression; when bandits are pacified in one place, rebels elsewhere dare not rise again;
translations.idiomatic: He urged that every governor focus on active suppression: once rebels were crushed in one sector, others would not dare rise;

sentences.zh: 鄰省賊滅，則本省之賊無自而來。

translations.literal: when bandits in a neighboring province are destroyed, the bandits of one's own province have no means by which to come.
translations.idiomatic: and when a neighboring province was cleared, one's own province would not be overrun from outside.

sentences.zh: 是不言防而防自固也。」

translations.literal: This is defense made secure without speaking of defense."
translations.idiomatic: That was how defenses would hold firm without endless talk of merely holding positions."

sentences.zh: 三月，揚州陷，茂廕疏言：「寇氛將偪山東，巡撫以勦賊出省，籓臬漫無佈置，城內團丁不滿七百。

translations.literal: In the third month Yangzhou fell; Maoyin memorialized: "The bandit atmosphere will soon press upon Shandong; the governor has left the province to suppress bandits, the provincial administration has made no arrangements at all, and the militia within the city number fewer than seven hundred.
translations.idiomatic: When Yangzhou fell in the third month, he warned that the rebels would soon threaten Shandong: the governor had marched out to fight them, the provincial staff had made no dispositions, and fewer than seven hundred militiamen remained in the city.

sentences.zh: 乞特簡重臣防守，以固畿南屏蔽。」

translations.literal: He begged that a specially selected senior minister be sent to defend, so as to secure the protective screen south of the capital region."
translations.idiomatic: He asked that a senior minister be appointed at once to hold the line and shield the approaches to the capital."

sentences.zh: 又言：「陝西設防，兵為民害，請諭飭按治。」

translations.literal: He also said: "In Shaanxi's establishment of defenses, the troops are a harm to the people; please issue instructions for investigation and punishment."
translations.idiomatic: He also reported that troops raised for defense in Shaanxi were oppressing the people and asked that the court order an investigation."

sentences.zh: 茂廕屢上疏，言事侃侃，文宗頗鄉用。

translations.literal: Maoyin repeatedly submitted memorials, speaking forthrightly on affairs; Emperor Wenzong was quite inclined to heed him.
translations.idiomatic: Maoyin memorialized repeatedly and spoke with frank conviction; Emperor Wenzong took his counsel seriously.

sentences.zh: 擢太常寺卿，遷太僕寺卿。

translations.literal: He was promoted to director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and transferred to director of the Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and then transferred to director of the Court of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 粵匪犯畿輔，參贊大臣科爾沁親王僧格林沁駐師涿州，諸軍咸觀望不肯前。

translations.literal: When the Cantonese rebels invaded the capital region, the assisting grand minister, Prince Sengge Rinchen of Horqin, stationed his army at Zhuozhou, and all the armies alike held back and would not advance.
translations.idiomatic: When the Taiping forces threatened the capital region, Prince Sengge Rinchen of Horqin encamped at Zhuozhou as assisting grand minister, while the other armies hung back and refused to advance.

sentences.zh: 茂廕疏言：「賊既渡滹沱而北，迴翔於深、晉之郊，而不遽北犯者，懼吾兵出也。

translations.literal: Maoyin memorialized: "The rebels having crossed the Hutuo northward, they wheel about in the suburbs of Shenzhou and Jizhou yet do not immediately invade northward because they fear our troops will come out.
translations.idiomatic: Maoyin wrote that after crossing the Hutuo River the rebels were circling the Shenzhou and Jizhou area yet hesitated to push north because they feared an imperial sortie.

sentences.zh: 吾兵出而遷延不進，賊有以知我之勇怯矣。

translations.literal: Our troops come out yet delay and do not advance; the rebels thereby learn whether we are brave or timid.
translations.idiomatic: If our armies march out but linger without attacking, the enemy will learn exactly how bold or timid we are.

sentences.zh: 臣竊謂賊自桂林北竄，諸帥喪師左次，皆為一守字所誤。

translations.literal: Your servant ventures to say that from the time the rebels fled north from Guilin, the commanders' loss of armies and halting in place have all been misled by the single word 'defend.'
translations.idiomatic: I believe that ever since the rebels fled north from Guilin, commanders who lost battles while merely holding their ground were all misled by obsession with defense.

sentences.zh: 賊屯一日，可資休息；

translations.literal: For each day the rebels encamp, they can rest and recover;
translations.idiomatic: Each day the rebels camp, they rest and recover;

sentences.zh: 我屯一日，銳氣日隳。

translations.literal: for each day we encamp, fighting spirit daily decays.
translations.idiomatic: each day we stand idle, our troops' morale decays further.

sentences.zh: 賊所過劫掠，行不裹糧；

translations.literal: Wherever the rebels pass they plunder and march without carrying provisions;
translations.idiomatic: They live off plunder wherever they march and carry no rations;

sentences.zh: 我軍坐食縣官，日需鉅餉。

translations.literal: our armies sit and eat at the expense of the district officials, daily requiring huge funds.
translations.idiomatic: while our armies sit in camp at public expense and consume vast sums every day.

sentences.zh: 相持數月，餉絕兵匱，不待交綏而勝負已判。

translations.literal: After facing each other for several months, funds are cut off and troops are exhausted; without waiting for battle, victory and defeat are already decided.
translations.idiomatic: After months of stalemate, funds run out and troops are exhausted; the outcome is decided before a battle is even fought.

sentences.zh: 請密飭王大臣等明發號令，按兵拒守，而陰選健將率死士數千，潛師出彼不意，麾兵急擊，一鼓可殲。

translations.literal: He requested that the princes and grand ministers be secretly ordered to issue open commands to hold the army on the defensive, while secretly selecting stalwart generals to lead several thousand death-defying troops, moving the army out where the enemy does not expect, commanding the troops in a swift attack, and destroying them in one drumbeat.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed that senior princes and ministers issue public orders to hold the line while secretly choosing bold generals to lead a few thousand picked men in a surprise strike that could wipe out the enemy in a single assault.

sentences.zh: 如此，則大河以南，諸賊心怵膽落，不敢复圖北犯矣。」

translations.literal: Thus, south of the Great River, all the rebels' hearts would be struck and their courage fall, and they would not dare again to plot a northern invasion."
translations.idiomatic: That would break the rebels' nerve south of the Yellow River and deter any further move toward the north."

sentences.zh: 尋命會辦京城團防保甲，擢戶部侍郎，兼管錢法堂。

translations.literal: Soon he was ordered to assist in managing the capital's militia defense and household registration system, was promoted to vice minister of revenue, and concurrently directed the Bureau of Currency.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon assigned to organize capital militia and household defense, promoted to vice minister of revenue, and put in charge of the Bureau of Currency.

sentences.zh: 戶部奏鑄當十、堂五十大錢，王大臣又請增鑄當百、當千，謂之四項大錢。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Revenue memorialized to cast ten-cash and fifty-cash large coins of the Bureau type; the princes and grand ministers further requested adding hundred-cash and thousand-cash issues, called the four kinds of large coin.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Revenue proposed casting ten- and fifty-cash large coins; senior princes and ministers then asked to add hundred- and thousand-cash pieces—the so-called four denominations of large cash.

sentences.zh: 當千者，以二兩為率，餘遞減。

translations.literal: For the thousand-cash piece, two taels was taken as the standard, with the rest decreasing in proportion.
translations.idiomatic: The thousand-cash coin was to contain two taels of metal by standard, with lower denominations scaled down accordingly.

sentences.zh: 茂廕上疏爭之曰：「大錢之鑄，意在節省，由漢訖明，行之屢矣。

translations.literal: Maoyin memorialized in opposition, saying: "Casting large coins is intended to economize; from Han through Ming it has been tried repeatedly.
translations.idiomatic: Maoyin protested in a memorial: "Large coins are meant to save copper; dynasties from Han through Ming have tried them again and again.

sentences.zh: 不久即廢，未能有經久者。

translations.literal: Before long they were abolished; none could endure for long.
translations.idiomatic: None lasted; every experiment was soon abandoned.

sentences.zh: 今行大錢，頗見便利，蓋喜新厭故，人情一概。

translations.literal: Now in issuing large coins they seem quite convenient, for people delight in the new and tire of the old—human sentiment is always the same.
translations.idiomatic: New large coins always seem convenient at first, for people tire of the old and flock to novelty.

sentences.zh: 及不旋踵，棄如敝屣。

translations.literal: Before one can turn the heel, they are cast aside like worn-out shoes.
translations.idiomatic: Almost at once they are cast aside like worn-out shoes.

sentences.zh: 稽諸往事，莫非如是。

translations.literal: Examining past affairs, none have failed to be thus.
translations.idiomatic: History shows the same pattern every time.

sentences.zh: 錢法過繁，市肆必擾，折當過重，廢罷必速，此人事物理之自然。

translations.literal: When the coinage system is too complex, markets are sure to be disturbed; when the exchange value is set too high, abolition comes swiftly—this is the natural course of human affairs and physical principle.
translations.idiomatic: Overly complex coinage disrupts trade; excessive face values lead to swift abolition—that is simply how markets and human nature work.

sentences.zh: 論者謂國家此制，當十則十，當千則千，孰敢有違？

translations.literal: Advocates say that under this state system, ten-cash means ten and thousand-cash means a thousand—who would dare disobey?
translations.idiomatic: Supporters argue that under state authority a ten-cash coin must count as ten and a thousand-cash as a thousand—who would dare refuse?

sentences.zh: 不知官能定錢直而不能定物直，錢當千，民不敢以為百；

translations.literal: They do not know that the government can fix the value of money but cannot fix the value of goods; when a coin is thousand-cash, the people dare not treat it as a hundred;
translations.idiomatic: They forget that government can fix nominal coin values but not prices: people will not treat a thousand-cash coin as worth a hundred;

sentences.zh: 物直百，民不難以為千。

translations.literal: when goods are worth a hundred, the people have no difficulty treating them as a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: but merchants will readily price a hundred-worth of goods at a thousand.

sentences.zh: 自來大錢之廢，多由私鑄繁興，物價騰踴。

translations.literal: Whenever large coins have been abolished, it has largely been because private casting flourished and commodity prices soared.
translations.idiomatic: Large coins have usually been abandoned because counterfeiting spread and prices soared.

sentences.zh: 宋沈畸之言曰：'當十錢鑄，召禍導姦，遊手之徒，爭先私鑄。

translations.literal: The Song official Shen Qi said: 'Casting ten-cash coins invites disaster and leads to villainy; idlers vie to cast privately first.'
translations.idiomatic: The Song official Shen Qi wrote that casting ten-cash coins 'invites calamity and encourages crime, as idlers rush to counterfeit them.'

sentences.zh: 無故而有數倍之息，雖日斬之，勢不可遏。

translations.literal: Without cause there is profit of several times; though one executes them daily, the momentum cannot be checked.
translations.idiomatic: When effortless profit runs to several times the cost, daily executions cannot stop it.

sentences.zh: '張方平之議曰：'奸人盜鑄，大錢之用日輕。

translations.literal: Zhang Fangping's proposal said: 'Villains secretly cast coins, and the use of large cash daily grows lighter.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Fangping argued that counterfeiters debased large coins day by day.

sentences.zh: 比年以來，虛高物估，增直於下，取償於上，有折當之虛名，罹虧損之實害。

translations.literal: In recent years commodity valuations have been falsely raised; value is increased below and compensation taken above—there is the empty name of exchange value, but the real harm of losses is suffered.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years prices were inflated on paper while merchants passed losses upward—nominal exchange rates masked real damage.

sentences.zh: '大觀錢鑄自蔡京，而其子絛作國史補敘：'始之得息流通，繼之盜鑄多弊，終之改當折閱。

translations.literal: The Daguang coins were cast under Cai Jing, and his son Cai Tao wrote in a supplement to the national history: 'At first profit was gained and they circulated; next secret casting brought many abuses; in the end the denomination was changed and they were discounted in depreciation.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Jing introduced the Daguang coins; his son Cai Tao recorded in a history supplement how they first circulated profitably, then succumbed to counterfeiting, and finally had to be revalued downward.

sentences.zh: '事皆目睹，尤為詳盡。

translations.literal: These matters were all witnessed by the eyes and are especially detailed.
translations.idiomatic: He had seen it all firsthand, and his account is especially telling.

sentences.zh: 古所不能行，而謂可通行於今乎？

translations.literal: What antiquity could not carry out—can one say it can be put into practice today?
translations.idiomatic: If it failed in antiquity, how can it work today?

sentences.zh: 信者國之寶。

translations.literal: Trust is the treasure of the state.
translations.idiomatic: Credibility is the state's greatest asset.

sentences.zh: 大錢鈔票，皆屬權宜之計，全在持之以信，庶可冀數年之利。

translations.literal: Large coins and paper notes are all expedients; everything depends on maintaining them with trust, so that one may hope for profit lasting several years.
translations.idiomatic: Large coins and paper notes are expedients that succeed only if the government keeps faith—then they might yield a few years' benefit.

sentences.zh: 今大錢輕重程式，甫經頒行，未及數月，忽盡更變。

translations.literal: Now the weight and standard of large coins have only just been promulgated; before several months had passed, they were suddenly all changed.
translations.idiomatic: The weight and standards for large coins had only just been issued; within months everything was changed again.

sentences.zh: 商民惶恐，群疑朝廷為不可信，此非細故也。

translations.literal: Merchants and people are fearful; all suspect that the court is untrustworthy—this is no small matter.
translations.idiomatic: Merchants are alarmed and doubt whether the court can be trusted—this is no trifling matter.

sentences.zh: 或慮銅短停鑄，故須及時變通，顧變通欲其能行，不行則亦與不鑄等。

translations.literal: Some fear a shortage of copper and cessation of casting, and therefore timely adaptation is needed; yet adaptation must be able to work—if it does not work, it is the same as not casting.
translations.idiomatic: Some argue that copper shortages require prompt adjustment—but adjustment only matters if it works; otherwise it is no better than stopping the mint altogether.

sentences.zh: 逆賊一平，不患無銅，若賊不能平，銅不能運，雖侭現有之銅，悉鑄當千，恐亦無濟，可慮者不僅停鑄而已。」

translations.literal: Once the rebellious bandits are pacified, one need not worry about lack of copper; if the bandits cannot be pacified and copper cannot be transported, even if all existing copper were cast into thousand-cash coins, I fear it would still not help—the worries are not only about stopping casting."
translations.idiomatic: Once the rebels are crushed, copper will not be lacking; if they are not crushed and copper cannot be moved, casting every available ingot into thousand-cash coins will not help—the problem is not merely a halt in minting."

sentences.zh: 上命王大臣及戶部秉公定議，王大臣終執原議。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered the princes and grand ministers and the Ministry of Revenue to deliberate impartially; the princes and grand ministers ultimately held to the original proposal.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered senior princes and the Ministry of Revenue to decide fairly, but the princes held to their original plan.

sentences.zh: 四年，戶部會奏推廣大錢辦法，茂廕复疏爭曰：「臣疏陳大錢利弊，未奉諭旨，臣職司錢法，夙夜思維，實覺難行。

translations.literal: In the fourth year the Ministry of Revenue jointly memorialized methods for extending large coins; Maoyin again memorialized in opposition, saying: "Your servant has memorialized on the advantages and disadvantages of large coins but has not received an imperial rescript; your servant's office oversees the currency system, and day and night in reflection I truly find it hard to implement.
translations.idiomatic: In 1854 the Ministry of Revenue memorialized jointly to expand large-coin policy; Maoyin protested again: "I have already explained the pros and cons of large coins without receiving a reply. As the official responsible for currency, I have thought on this day and night and find the policy unworkable.

sentences.zh: 當百以上大錢，與原行當五十者無甚分別，此何以貴，彼何以賤，難一；

translations.literal: Hundred-cash and higher large coins differ little from the originally issued fifty-cash pieces—why should these be valued high and those valued low? Difficulty one;
translations.idiomatic: Hundred-cash and higher denominations differ little from the existing fifty-cash coins—why should one be prized and the other cheap? That is the first difficulty;

sentences.zh: 以易市物，則難分折，以易制錢，莫與兌換，難二；

translations.literal: in exchanging for market goods, change is hard to make; in exchanging for standard cash, none will redeem them—difficulty two;
translations.idiomatic: they are awkward in trade and cannot be exchanged for standard cash—the second difficulty;

sentences.zh: 大錢雖準交官項，然準交五成者，已有寶鈔官票，大錢何能並搭？

translations.literal: Although large coins are permitted for official payments, for payments permitted at fifty percent there are already treasure notes and official bills—how can large coins be used together?
translations.idiomatic: although large coins may pay certain official dues, treasury notes already cover the fifty-percent quota—how can large coins be piled on top? That is the third difficulty.

sentences.zh: 難三。

translations.literal: Difficulty three.
translations.idiomatic: The third difficulty.

sentences.zh: 此猶其小者耳，最大之患，莫如私鑄。

translations.literal: These are still the lesser matters; the greatest calamity is none other than private casting.
translations.idiomatic: These are minor problems beside the greatest danger: counterfeiting.

sentences.zh: 奸人以銅四兩鑄大錢兩枚，即抵交官銀一兩，是病國也。

translations.literal: Villains with four taels of copper cast two large coins and thereby pay one tael of official silver—this harms the state.
translations.idiomatic: Counterfeiters can cast two large coins from four taels of copper and tender them as one tael of official silver—a direct injury to the state.

sentences.zh: 蓋行制錢，每千重百二十兩，鎔之可得六十兩，以鑄當十錢可得三十千。

translations.literal: For circulating standard cash, each thousand weighs one hundred twenty taels; melted down they yield sixty taels, and cast into ten-cash coins they can obtain thirty thousand cash.
translations.idiomatic: A thousand standard cash coins weigh 120 taels; melted down they yield 60 taels of copper, which counterfeiters can turn into 30,000 cash worth of ten-cash coins.

sentences.zh: 設奸人日銷制錢以鑄大錢，民間將無制錢可用，是病民也。

translations.literal: If villains daily melt standard cash to cast large coins, the people will have no standard cash to use—this harms the people.
translations.idiomatic: If counterfeiters daily melt standard cash into large coins, the people will be left without usable small change—that harms the populace.

sentences.zh: 寶鈔官票，其省遠過大錢，果能推行盡利，裨益亦非淺鮮，大錢之行，似可已也。」

translations.literal: Treasure notes and official bills economize far more than large coins; if they can truly be extended to full benefit, the gain is also not slight—issuing large coins seems something that can be stopped."
translations.idiomatic: Treasury notes save far more than large coins; if they are fully implemented the benefit will be great, and large coins might well be discontinued."

sentences.zh: 疏入，仍不報。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted but still received no response.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial went in, but again there was no reply.

sentences.zh: 其後大錢終廢，如茂廕言。

translations.literal: Afterward large coins were finally abolished, as Maoyin had said.
translations.idiomatic: Large coins were eventually abolished, just as Maoyin had predicted.

sentences.zh: 又疏論鈔法利病，略曰：「上年初用銀鈔，雖未暢行，亦未滋累。

translations.literal: He again memorialized on the advantages and disadvantages of the note system, saying in summary: "In the first year of the reign silver notes were first used; though they did not circulate freely, they also did not breed burdens.
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized on paper currency, noting that when silver notes were first introduced the previous year they had not circulated widely but had not yet caused serious harm.

sentences.zh: 及臘月行錢鈔，至今已發百數十萬，為累頗多。

translations.literal: When cash notes were issued in the twelfth month, up to now more than a million and several hundred thousand have been issued, and the burdens are quite numerous.
translations.idiomatic: After cash notes were issued in the twelfth month, more than a million had already been put out, with troubling consequences.

sentences.zh: 向來鈔法，唐、宋之飛錢、交子、會子，皆有實以運之。

translations.literal: In past note systems, the Tang and Song flying money, jiaozi, and huizi all had substance to move them.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier note systems—from Tang and Song flying money, jiaozi, and huizi—were all backed by real reserves.

sentences.zh: 元廢銀錢不用而專用鈔，上下通行，為能以虛運實。

translations.literal: The Yuan abolished silver and cash and used only notes; they circulated above and below, and thus could use the insubstantial to move the substantial.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuan abolished silver and coin in favor of notes alone; because they circulated throughout society, the insubstantial could mobilize the substantial.

sentences.zh: 明專以虛責民，以實歸上，勢遂不行。

translations.literal: The Ming used the insubstantial solely to burden the people and the substantial to return to the court; the momentum therefore could not be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: The Ming used paper to burden the people while hoarding metal for the state, and the system therefore failed.

sentences.zh: 臣元年所奏，皆以實運虛之法。

translations.literal: What your servant memorialized in the first year of the reign was entirely the method of using the substantial to move the insubstantial.
translations.idiomatic: What I proposed in the first year of the reign was precisely the method of backing notes with real assets.

sentences.zh: 今時勢所迫，前法不行，議者雖專於收鈔時設法，然京師放多收少，軍營有放無收，直省州縣有收無放，非有商人運於其間，則皆不行。

translations.literal: Now compelled by the times, the former method cannot be carried out; though advocates focus on devising methods when receiving notes, in the capital more is issued than received, in military camps there is issue without receipt, and in provinces and districts there is receipt without issue—unless merchants transport between them, none of it can work.
translations.idiomatic: Circumstances now forbid the old approach; though reformers focus on collection rules, Beijing issues more than it takes in, camps pay out without recalling notes, and provinces collect without paying out—without merchants to move notes between them, nothing works.

sentences.zh: 非與商人以可運之方、能運之利，亦仍不能行。」

translations.literal: Unless merchants are given a means by which notes can be transported and a profit by which they can transport them, it still cannot work."
translations.idiomatic: Unless merchants are given both a practical way to move notes and a profit in doing so, the system will still fail."

sentences.zh: 因擬上四事，務在通商情，利轉運。

translations.literal: He therefore drafted four proposals, aiming to open commercial sentiment and benefit transport.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore proposed four measures designed to align with commercial practice and facilitate circulation.

sentences.zh: 奏入，上斥其為商人指使，不關心於國是，命恭親王奕訢、定郡王載銓覈議。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, the emperor rebuked him as directed by merchants and unconcerned with state affairs, and ordered Prince Gong Yixin and Prince Ding Zaiquan to examine and deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rejected the memorial as merchant-driven and indifferent to state policy, and ordered Prince Gong Yixin and Prince Ding Zaiquan to review it.

sentences.zh: 議上，謂茂廕所論，窒礙難行，嚴旨切責。

translations.literal: When their deliberation was submitted, they said Maoyin's proposals were obstructive and hard to implement; a stern edict sharply rebuked him.
translations.idiomatic: Their report declared Maoyin's proposals impracticable, and the emperor issued a stern rebuke.

sentences.zh: 尋調兵部。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 粵匪踞池州、太平，皖南隔絕，茂廕奏請以徽州暫歸浙江統轄，上命浙江巡撫黃宗漢體察酌行。

translations.literal: The Cantonese rebels held Chizhou and Taiping; southern Anhui was cut off; Maoyin memorialized requesting that Huizhou temporarily be placed under Zhejiang's jurisdiction; the emperor ordered the Zhejiang governor Huang Zonghan to investigate and act as appropriate.
translations.idiomatic: With Taiping forces holding Chizhou and Taiping and southern Anhui cut off, Maoyin asked that Huizhou be temporarily placed under Zhejiang; the emperor told Governor Huang Zonghan of Zhejiang to investigate and decide.

sentences.zh: 初，茂廕疏言：「賊脅良民，驅為前鋒。

translations.literal: Earlier Maoyin had memorialized: "The rebels coerce good people and drive them as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier he had written that the rebels coerced ordinary people and drove them as front-line fodder.

sentences.zh: 請特降諭旨，自拔來歸，均從寬貸。

translations.literal: He requested a special imperial edict that those who break away and come over of themselves should all receive lenient pardon.
translations.idiomatic: He asked for an edict promising leniency to anyone who deserted and came over voluntarily.

sentences.zh: 殺賊來獻，均加爵賞。」

translations.literal: Those who kill rebels and come to offer their heads should all receive enfeoffment and reward."
translations.idiomatic: Those who killed rebels and defected should receive titles and rewards."

sentences.zh: 京師久不雨，上命清釐庶獄，減免情節可矜者，茂廕又疏言：「可矜者莫如賊中逃出之難民，各處捕獲難民，指為形跡可疑，嚴訊楚毒。

translations.literal: When the capital had long been without rain, the emperor ordered a clearing of ordinary prisons and mitigation for cases with pitiable circumstances; Maoyin again memorialized: "The most pitiable are refugees who escaped from among the bandits; refugees captured everywhere are accused of suspicious conduct and severely interrogated with cruel torture.
translations.idiomatic: During a prolonged drought in the capital, the emperor ordered a review of ordinary prisons and clemency for deserving cases; Maoyin wrote that the most deserving were refugees who had fled the rebels, yet captives everywhere were tortured on suspicion.

sentences.zh: 此輩於法不為無罪，於情實有可矜，請敕暫緩定擬。

translations.literal: These people are not without guilt under the law, yet in sentiment they are truly pitiable; I request an edict to suspend final judgment temporarily.
translations.idiomatic: They were not legally innocent, yet morally deserving of mercy; he asked that sentencing be postponed.

sentences.zh: 皇上御極以來，屢詔求言，言或無當，奉旨明斥；

translations.literal: Since Your Majesty ascended the throne, edicts have repeatedly sought counsel; when counsel was sometimes inappropriate, an edict clearly rebuked it;
translations.idiomatic: Since Your Majesty's accession you have repeatedly called for frank counsel; when advice missed the mark, edicts rebuked it plainly;

sentences.zh: 斥其無當，非禁使不言也，然言者即因以見少。

translations.literal: rebuking what was inappropriate was not forbidding people to speak, yet those who spoke therefore became few.
translations.idiomatic: rebuking bad advice was not forbidding speech, yet memorialists grew scarce nonetheless.

sentences.zh: 即如諸路僨軍失地之將帥，未敗之始，其措置乖方，人言藉藉；

translations.literal: Take, for example, the commanders on various routes who exhausted armies and lost territory—before defeat their dispositions were perverse and public talk was widespread;
translations.idiomatic: Consider the generals who squandered armies and lost territory: long before defeat their conduct was widely criticized;

sentences.zh: 而無敢為皇上言者，或慮無實據也，或雖有實據而慮查辦時化為子虛也，或慮不用而徒招怨也，或謂聖心自有權衡也，是以皆不敢言。

translations.literal: yet none dared speak to the emperor—some feared lack of solid evidence, some feared that even with evidence an investigation would turn it into nothing, some feared that if not adopted they would only invite resentment, and some said the sacred mind had its own balance—so all dared not speak.
translations.idiomatic: yet no one dared tell the emperor: some feared lacking proof, others that investigations would erase the facts, others that speaking would invite resentment without effect, and still others that the emperor already knew—so all held their tongues.

sentences.zh: 至用人進退之際，臣子每不敢盡言，淺者懼幹聖怒而見斥，深者懼激上意而難回。

translations.literal: At moments of appointment and dismissal, ministers often do not dare speak fully; the shallow fear provoking imperial anger and dismissal, the deep fear arousing the sovereign's will so that it cannot be turned back.
translations.idiomatic: On appointments and dismissals, officials rarely speak plainly: the timid fear imperial wrath, the thoughtful fear provoking a decision that cannot be reversed.

sentences.zh: 皇上披覽奏章，纖悉必邀批示，勤亦至矣。

translations.literal: When Your Majesty peruses memorials, the smallest detail must receive a rescript—diligence has reached its utmost.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty reads every memorial in detail and marks every point—no ruler could be more diligent.

sentences.zh: 臣以為精神貴於不紛，原務其遠者大者，捨其近者小者。

translations.literal: Your servant believes that spirit is precious when not scattered; one should attend to what is distant and great, and set aside what is near and small.
translations.idiomatic: I believe the sovereign's attention should not be scattered on trifles but reserved for great matters of long-term consequence.

sentences.zh: 明主勞於求賢，而逸於任人。

translations.literal: An enlightened ruler toils at seeking the worthy and rests in employing them.
translations.idiomatic: A wise ruler labors to find talent and then trusts it to work.

sentences.zh: 今天下人才不足，此誠可憂。

translations.literal: Today talent under Heaven is insufficient—this is truly worrisome.
translations.idiomatic: The empire today lacks capable men, and that is a genuine cause for alarm.

sentences.zh: 雖然，非無才也。

translations.literal: Even so, there is no lack of talent.
translations.idiomatic: Yet talent is not truly absent.

sentences.zh: 如羅澤南，人無不知為將材矣，初不過一貢生耳。

translations.literal: Such as Luo Zexian—everyone knows he is material for a general, yet at first he was nothing but a tribute student.
translations.idiomatic: Take Luo Zexian: everyone recognized his military gifts, yet he began as nothing more than a tribute student.

sentences.zh: 湖南一省，既有江忠源兄弟，又有羅澤南諸人，則他省可知。

translations.literal: In Hunan province alone there are both the Jiang brothers and men like Luo Zexian—then other provinces may be known.
translations.idiomatic: Hunan alone produced the Jiang brothers and men like Luo Zexian; other provinces surely hold similar men.

sentences.zh: 惟賢知賢，惟才愛才，是在聖心之誠求耳。

translations.literal: Only the worthy know the worthy; only talent loves talent—this lies in the sincere seeking of the sacred heart.
translations.idiomatic: Only the worthy recognize worth, and only talent cherishes talent—the question is whether the throne seeks them sincerely.

sentences.zh: 方今武昌未下，江西又復危急，兩省之民，向也與賊為仇，今乃竟有從逆者。

translations.literal: Now Wuchang is not yet taken and Jiangxi is again critically endangered; the people of the two provinces, who once were enemies of the bandits, now actually have some who follow the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Wuchang remains untaken and Jiangxi is again in peril; people who once hated the rebels are now joining them.

sentences.zh: 此中轉移之故，宜深思也。

translations.literal: The cause of this shift should be deeply pondered.
translations.idiomatic: The reasons for this reversal deserve deep reflection.

sentences.zh: 列聖仁漸德被，人心斷不能忘。

translations.literal: The successive sage emperors' benevolence gradually spread and virtue covered all; the people's hearts assuredly cannot forget.
translations.idiomatic: The benevolence of successive emperors has long won the people's hearts, and they cannot have forgotten it.

sentences.zh: 然此時不亟維繫，使賊得徐出假仁假義以為市，恐民心將為所搖而難挽矣。」

translations.literal: Yet if at this time one does not urgently bind them together, allowing the bandits slowly to offer false benevolence and false righteousness as a market, I fear popular hearts will be swayed and hard to recover."
translations.idiomatic: Yet unless we act now, the rebels may win people over with sham benevolence—and popular loyalty may slip beyond recovery."

sentences.zh: 奏入，上嘉納之。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, the emperor praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor welcomed the memorial and approved its advice.

sentences.zh: 八年，病免。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was dismissed on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In 1858 he retired because of illness.

sentences.zh: 十一年，穆宗即位，以茂廕忠直，命俟病痊聽候簡用。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, when Emperor Muzong ascended the throne, because Maoyin was loyal and upright, he was ordered to await selection once his illness healed.
translations.idiomatic: In 1861, when Emperor Tongzhi ascended the throne, Maoyin was ordered to await appointment once he recovered, in recognition of his integrity.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，上疏陳時政，言：「天象示警，宜廑修省。

translations.literal: In the first year of the Tongzhi reign he memorialized on current policy, saying: "Heaven's signs warn; one should be diligent in self-examination.
translations.idiomatic: In 1862 he memorialized on state affairs, urging that heavenly warnings called for moral self-scrutiny at court.

sentences.zh: 議政王責任重大，宜專心機務，餘事綜其大綱。

translations.literal: The Prince Regent bears heavy responsibility and should concentrate on affairs of state, leaving other matters to their broad outlines.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince Regent should focus on major policy and leave lesser matters to subordinates.

sentences.zh: 言官宜加優容。

translations.literal: Censors should receive greater forbearance.
translations.idiomatic: Memorialists and censors should be treated with greater tolerance.

sentences.zh: 順天府事繁，府尹石贊清不宜兼部。

translations.literal: The Shuntian prefecture has heavy business; the prefect Shi Zanqing should not concurrently hold a ministry post.
translations.idiomatic: Shuntian prefecture is overburdened; Prefect Shi Zanqing should not also hold a ministry appointment.

sentences.zh: 各國通商事務衙門司員甫及一年，即得優保，恐各衙門人員皆以營求保送為得計，宜防其漸。」

translations.literal: Staff of the Yamen for the Management of Affairs of All Nations had served barely a year when they received favorable recommendations; I fear personnel in every yamen will regard seeking such promotion as their plan—one should guard against this gradual trend."
translations.idiomatic: Clerks in the foreign affairs yamen were promoted after only a year; if every office follows that path, merit will give way to patronage."

sentences.zh: 署左副都御史，命偕兵部尚書愛仁往山西按事。

translations.literal: He served as acting left vice censor-in-chief and was ordered together with the minister of war Airen to go to Shanxi to investigate affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed acting left vice censor-in-chief and sent with Minister of War Airen to investigate affairs in Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 授工部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was appointed vice minister of works.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed vice minister of works.

sentences.zh: 二年，調吏部。

translations.literal: In the second year he was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In 1863 he was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 丁繼母憂，歸。

translations.literal: He mourned his stepmother and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: After his stepmother died he returned home to observe mourning.

sentences.zh: 四年，卒於家。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home in 1865.

sentences.zh: =宋晉=宋晉，字錫蕃，江蘇溧陽人。

translations.literal: Song Jin, courtesy name Xifan, was a native of Liyang in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Song Jin, whose courtesy name was Xifan, came from Liyang in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 道光二十四年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year of the Daoguang reign he passed the jinshi examination, was selected as a bachelor of the Hanlin Academy, and was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in 1844, entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, and was appointed a compiler.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，大考二等，擢中允。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year, in the great examination he placed second class and was promoted to palace expositor.
translations.idiomatic: In 1847 he placed second class in the palace examination and was promoted to palace expositor.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，典河南鄉試，因命題錯誤議處，諭不得更與考試差。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year he presided over the Henan provincial examination; because of an error in the examination topic he was disciplined and ordered never again to receive examination assignments.
translations.idiomatic: In 1849 he served as chief examiner for Henan but was punished for an erroneous examination topic and barred from future examining posts.

sentences.zh: 咸豐二年，大考二等，擢侍讀學士，遷光祿寺卿。

translations.literal: In the second year of the Xianfeng reign, in the great examination he placed second class and was promoted to reader of the Hanlin Academy, then transferred to director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: In 1852 he again placed second class in the palace examination, was promoted to Hanlin reader, and then became director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 三年，命會辦京城團防保甲，署禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the third year he was ordered to assist in managing the capital's militia defense and household registration system, and served as acting vice minister of rites.
translations.idiomatic: In 1853 he was assigned to help organize capital militia and household defense and served as acting vice minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 四年正月，疏言：「去冬圜丘大祭，適值聖體違和，禮臣以登降繁縟，於親詣壇位及奠帛後諸儀節，更加酌定，奏請允行，旋以遣親王恭代而止。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourth year he memorialized: "Last winter at the great suburban sacrifice at the Round Mound, it happened that the sacred person was unwell; the ritual officials, because ascending and descending were elaborate, further adjusted several ceremonial points after the emperor's personal approach to the altar and after the offering of silks, memorialized for approval, and soon it stopped with dispatching an imperial prince to substitute by reverent proxy.
translations.idiomatic: In early 1854 he memorialized that during the previous winter's Round Mound sacrifice the emperor had been unwell; ritual officials had simplified several steps and sought approval, but in the end a prince substituted for the emperor.

sentences.zh: 惟詳稽典禮，祀天鉅典，尤為慎重。

translations.literal: Only upon detailed examination of canonical ritual is the great ceremony of sacrificing to Heaven especially grave.
translations.idiomatic: Canonical ritual shows that sacrifice to Heaven is the gravest ceremony of all.

sentences.zh: 偶遇服色不宜，興居未適，有遣代，無議減。

translations.literal: If by chance dress color is unsuitable or rising and dwelling are not fitting, there is dispatching a substitute, but no discussion of reduction.
translations.idiomatic: When dress or condition is unsuitable, emperors send substitutes—but they do not reduce the rite.

sentences.zh: 現值祈年大祀，伏原皇上飭停新議，仍遵成憲。」

translations.literal: Now that the great sacrifice for praying for the year is at hand, I bow and beg Your Majesty to order a halt to the new proposals and still follow the established statutes."
translations.idiomatic: With the annual prayer-for-harvest sacrifice approaching, he begged the emperor to abandon the new proposals and follow established ritual."

sentences.zh: 五年，遷宗人府丞。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was transferred to vice director of the Imperial Clan Court.
translations.idiomatic: In 1855 he was transferred to vice director of the Imperial Clan Court.

sentences.zh: 六年，疏言：「自江寧失陷，上自九江，下及鎮江、瓜洲，寇勢水陸相援。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he memorialized: "Since Jiangning fell, from Jiujiang above to Zhenjiang and Guazhou below, the bandit force supports itself by land and water.
translations.idiomatic: In 1856 he wrote that since Nanjing fell, rebels controlled the Yangzi from Jiujiang to Zhenjiang and Guazhou by land and water.

sentences.zh: 現聞向榮兵力不支，情形危急，今即分路赴援，仍恐緩不濟事。

translations.literal: It is now heard that Xiang Rong's military strength cannot sustain itself and the situation is critically dangerous; even if troops are sent by separate routes to aid, I still fear it will be too slow to help.
translations.idiomatic: He reported that Xiang Rong's forces were failing and the situation desperate; divided relief columns would arrive too late.

sentences.zh: 請飭江督、浙撫，僱用輪船載兵，由圌山關入江，焚攻金、焦賊船。

translations.literal: I request that the Jiangsu governor-general and Zhejiang governor be ordered to hire steamships to carry troops, enter the Yangzi through Tushan Pass, and burn and attack the bandit ships at Jinshan and Jiaoshan.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed that Jiangsu and Zhejiang hire steamers to carry troops through Tushan Pass and burn rebel vessels at Jinshan and Jiaoshan.

sentences.zh: 再由儀徵溯浦口，與六合諸軍相為犄角，則江寧、鎮江對岸之賊，節節防我，必不敢離巢東竄。

translations.literal: Then from Yizheng go upriver to Pukou and coordinate with the armies of Luhe in mutual support; then the bandits on the opposite bank from Jiangning and Zhenjiang, section by section defending against us, will surely not dare leave their nests and flee east.
translations.idiomatic: From Yizheng they could move upriver to Pukou and coordinate with Luhe forces, pinning rebels on the north bank and preventing an eastward breakout.

sentences.zh: 是不特解江南之急，即江北亦愈寧謐。

translations.literal: Thus not only is the urgency of Jiangnan relieved, but north of the river also becomes more tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: That would ease the crisis in Jiangnan and stabilize the north bank as well.

sentences.zh: 又聞廣東新至紅單船二十餘艘，請飭德興阿、向榮將紅單船並歸一處，力扼蕪湖江面。

translations.literal: It is also heard that more than twenty red-barbarian ships have newly arrived from Guangdong; I request that De Xing'a and Xiang Rong gather the red-barbarian ships in one place and forcefully block the Wuhu river surface.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked that twenty-odd foreign steamers newly arrived from Guangdong be concentrated under De Xing'a and Xiang Rong to block the river at Wuhu.

sentences.zh: 如能克復蕪湖，則拊賊之背，寧國不攻自下。」

translations.literal: If Wuhu can be recovered, then striking the bandits' rear, Ningguo will fall without attack."
translations.idiomatic: Recovering Wuhu would strike the rebels from behind and bring Ningguo without a siege."

sentences.zh: 薦道員繆梓、楊裕深、金安清通達治體，洞悉夷情，請以僱船籌費諸事責成辦理。

translations.literal: He recommended the circuit intendants Miu Zi, Yang Yushen, and Jin Anqing as penetrating statecraft and thoroughly understanding barbarian conditions, and requested that matters of hiring ships and raising funds be entrusted to them for completion.
translations.idiomatic: He recommended circuit officials Miu Zi, Yang Yushen, and Jin Anqing as men who understood governance and foreign affairs, and asked that hiring ships and raising funds be entrusted to them.

sentences.zh: 疏上，諭兩江總督怡良與向榮、德興阿酌行。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, an edict ordered the governor-general of the two Jiangs Yi Liang to deliberate and act with Xiang Rong and De Xing'a.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Governor-General Yi Liang to consult Xiang Rong and De Xing'a and act accordingly.

sentences.zh: 宣宗實錄告成，敘勞，擢內閣學士，迭署戶、工二部侍郎。

translations.literal: When the Veritable Records of Emperor Xuanzong were completed, he was rewarded for labor and promoted to grand secretary of the Grand Secretariat, successively serving as acting vice minister of revenue and of works.
translations.idiomatic: When the Veritable Records of Emperor Daoguang were completed, he was promoted to grand secretary and served acting terms in the Ministries of Revenue and Works.

sentences.zh: 八年，授工部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was appointed vice minister of works.
translations.idiomatic: In 1858 he was appointed vice minister of works.

sentences.zh: 文宗頻歲抱病，未能親行祀典，十年，晉疏言：「近年郊​​壇大祀，聖躬以步履失常，偶緩親行，而於遣恭代外，仍先期躬詣皇乾殿拈香，仰見寅畏深衷。

translations.literal: Emperor Wenzong was ill for successive years and could not personally perform the sacrificial ceremonies; in the tenth year Jin memorialized: "In recent years at the great suburban sacrifices at the suburban altars, the sacred person, because gait was abnormal, occasionally delayed personal attendance; yet apart from dispatching reverent substitution, he still beforehand in person went to the Huangqian Hall to draw incense—I have seen the profound reverence in his heart.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianfeng had been ill for years and could not attend sacrifices in person; in 1860 Song Jin noted that though princes often substituted, the emperor still went in person to offer incense at Huangqian Hall beforehand, showing deep reverence.

sentences.zh: 惟每屆大祀，皇上於前一日辰巳間躬詣拈香，即在齋宮祇宿。

translations.literal: Only at each great sacrifice, on the day before, between the chen and si hours the emperor in person went to draw incense and lodged in the fasting palace.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, on the eve of each great sacrifice, the emperor offered incense between mid-morning and noon and stayed in the fasting palace.

sentences.zh: 今則先期即如臨事，請於前一日寅卯間先行詣殿拈香，然後還宮辦事。

translations.literal: Now he acts beforehand as if the ceremony were at hand; I request that on the day before, between the yin and mao hours, he first go to the hall to draw incense and then return to the palace to conduct affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Now the emperor was treating the eve like the day itself; he proposed incense between early morning hours, then a return to the palace.

sentences.zh: 臣尤原慎攝聖躬，養元氣，節峻伐之味，復健行之常，於下屆郊祀大典照常親行。」

translations.literal: Your servant further wishes careful preservation of the sacred person, nourishing vital energy, moderating harsh medicinals, restoring the norm of vigorous walking, and at the next suburban sacrifice great ceremony personally attending as usual."
translations.idiomatic: He also urged the emperor to conserve his health, moderate harsh medicines, regain strength, and personally attend the next suburban sacrifice."

sentences.zh: 上嘉納之。

translations.literal: The emperor praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved his advice.

sentences.zh: 十一年，疏言：「江寧失陷已將十載，總督曾國籓經營防剿，與官文、胡林翼會合攻復安慶，惟所部不足二萬人。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he memorialized: "Jiangning has been lost for nearly ten years; Governor-General Zeng Guofan has managed defense and suppression, and with Guan Wen and Hu Linyi jointly attacked and recovered Anqing, yet his forces number fewer than twenty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: In 1861 he wrote that Nanjing had been lost nearly ten years; Zeng Guofan had recovered Anqing with Guan Wen and Hu Linyi but commanded fewer than twenty thousand men.

sentences.zh: 若合四川、湖北、湖南、江西、安徽五省歲入，養兵勇十三萬人，以七萬分駐防剿，六萬大舉東征，餉足兵增，庶可一舉集事。」

translations.literal: If the annual revenues of the five provinces Sichuan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, and Anhui were combined to support one hundred thirty thousand soldiers, with seventy thousand stationed for defense and suppression and sixty thousand making a great eastern expedition, with funds sufficient and troops increased, then perhaps in one move the affair could be settled."
translations.idiomatic: He proposed funding 130,000 troops from five provinces—70,000 for garrison duty and 60,000 for a major eastern campaign—so that adequate pay might finish the war in one stroke."

sentences.zh: 又言：「江西首當賊衝，巡撫毓科、布政使慶善皆失人望，請以太常寺卿左宗棠簡署巡撫，而於督糧道李桓、前廣饒道沈葆楨、浙江道員史致諤三人中簡擇擢授籓司。」

translations.literal: He also said: "Jiangxi is foremost where the bandits strike; Governor Yu Ke and provincial administration commissioner Qing Shan have both lost public confidence; I request that Zuo Zongtang, director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, be simply appointed acting governor, and that one of the three—grain transport commissioner Li Huan, former circuit intendant of Guangrao Shen Baozhen, and Zhejiang circuit intendant Shi Zhiyu—be selected and promoted as provincial administration commissioner."
translations.idiomatic: He urged replacing the discredited Jiangxi governor and administration commissioner with Zuo Zongtang as acting governor and selecting a strong provincial administration commissioner from Li Huan, Shen Baozhen, or Shi Zhiyu."

sentences.zh: 又請以曾國籓總統四川、湖北、湖南、江西、安徽五省督辦東征軍務。

translations.literal: He also requested that Zeng Guofan be made overall commander of military affairs for the eastern expedition in the five provinces Sichuan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, and Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked that Zeng Guofan be given overall command of the eastern campaign across those five provinces.

sentences.zh: 上以所籌不為無見，下官文、國籓等議奏。

translations.literal: The emperor said his planning was not without insight and referred it to Guan Wen, Guofan, and others for joint memorial.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor found merit in the plan and ordered Guan Wen, Zeng Guofan, and others to report jointly.

sentences.zh: 又疏言：「慕陵規制，儉約樸實，萬世可法。

translations.literal: He again memorialized: "The regulations of the Mu Mausoleum are frugal, simple, and solid—a model for ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: He also urged that the Mu Mausoleum's frugal design should remain the eternal model.

sentences.zh: 定陵工程請仿行勿改。」

translations.literal: The Ding Mausoleum project should be carried out in imitation without change."
translations.idiomatic: The Ding Mausoleum should follow the same restrained design."

sentences.zh: 格於部議，不行。

translations.literal: It was blocked by ministry deliberation and not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: The ministries rejected the proposal.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，調倉場侍郎。

translations.literal: In the first year of the Tongzhi reign he was transferred to vice minister of the grain transport.
translations.idiomatic: In 1862 he was transferred to vice minister of grain transport.

sentences.zh: 南漕初改海運，歲額三百萬石，自天津運京倉，偷漏飛灑，歲損米綦鉅。

translations.literal: Southern tribute grain was first changed to sea transport; the annual quota was three million shi; from Tianjin to the capital granaries, theft, leakage, and scattering lost grain in enormous amounts each year.
translations.idiomatic: When southern grain tribute shifted to sea transport, three million shi were due annually, yet enormous quantities were lost to theft and spillage between Tianjin and Beijing.

sentences.zh: 迨軍興，江、浙郡邑淪陷，南漕起運才二十餘萬石，而偷漏飛灑如故。

translations.literal: When the military campaigns began, Jiangsu and Zhejiang prefectures and districts fell; southern tribute grain shipped was only a little more than two hundred thousand shi, yet theft, leakage, and scattering remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: After Jiangsu and Zhejiang fell in the war, only about 200,000 shi were shipped, while losses continued unchanged.

sentences.zh: 十年以來，侍郎及監督官凡數易。

translations.literal: Over more than ten years, vice ministers and supervising officials changed several times.
translations.idiomatic: Over more than ten years, the responsible vice ministers and supervisors changed repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 晉受事，深悉其弊，因循未奏舉。

translations.literal: When Jin took office he knew the abuses deeply but followed precedent and did not memorialize impeachments.
translations.idiomatic: Jin understood the abuses well but, following precedent, did not report them.

sentences.zh: 六年，事發，左遷內閣學士，償米二萬石。

translations.literal: In the sixth year the affair broke out; he was demoted to grand secretary of the Grand Secretariat and required to compensate twenty thousand shi of grain.
translations.idiomatic: In 1867 the scandal broke; he was demoted to grand secretary and ordered to compensate 20,000 shi of grain.

sentences.zh: 十二年，遷戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was transferred to vice minister of revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In 1873 he was transferred to vice minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 十三年，卒。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 1874.

sentences.zh: =袁希祖=袁希祖，字荀陔，湖北漢陽人，原籍浙江上虞。

translations.literal: Yuan Xizu, courtesy name Xungai, was a native of Hanyang in Hubei, with original household registration in Shangyu, Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Xizu, whose courtesy name was Xungai, was registered in Hanyang, Hubei, though his ancestral home was Shangyu in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 道光二十七年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year of the Daoguang reign he passed the jinshi examination, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, and was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi in 1847, entered the Hanlin Academy, and became a compiler.

sentences.zh: 咸豐二年，大考二等，擢侍講。

translations.literal: In the second year of the Xianfeng reign, in the great examination he placed second class and was promoted to Hanlin expositor.
translations.idiomatic: In 1852 he placed second class in the palace examination and was promoted to Hanlin expositor.

sentences.zh: 三遷侍講學士。

translations.literal: He was transferred three times to reader of the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through three promotions to Hanlin reader.

sentences.zh: 八年，超擢內閣學士。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was exceptionally promoted to grand secretary of the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In 1858 he was exceptionally promoted to grand secretary.

sentences.zh: 迭署禮、工、刑諸部侍郎。

translations.literal: He successively served as acting vice minister of rites, works, and punishment.
translations.idiomatic: He served acting terms as vice minister of rites, works, and punishment.

sentences.zh: 九年，疏言：「咸豐初以道梗銅少，改鑄大錢，未幾，當百、當五皆不行，惟當十行之。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he memorialized: "At the beginning of the Xianfeng reign, because roads were blocked and copper was scarce, large coins were cast; before long, hundred-cash and five-cash issues did not circulate—only ten-cash circulated.
translations.idiomatic: In 1859 he wrote that early Xianfeng coinage had introduced large coins; hundred- and five-cash pieces failed, leaving only ten-cash coins in use.

sentences.zh: 始直制錢三五，近則以十當一。

translations.literal: At first they were worth three to five standard cash; recently ten are taken for one.
translations.idiomatic: At first a ten-cash coin traded for three to five standard cash; now ten are needed for one.

sentences.zh: 銀直增貴，百​​物騰踴，民間重困。

translations.literal: Silver grew more costly and all commodities soared; the people were heavily distressed.
translations.idiomatic: Silver rose in price, goods soared, and the people were crushed.

sentences.zh: 旗餉月三兩，改折錢十五千，致無以自活。

translations.literal: Banner pay of three taels a month was converted to fifteen thousand cash, so that they could not support themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Bannermen's monthly three-tael stipends were paid in cash at a rate of 15,000 cash, leaving them unable to live.

sentences.zh: 向日制錢重一錢二分，大錢重四錢八分，以之當十，贏五錢四分。

translations.literal: Formerly standard cash weighed one mace and two candareens; large coins weighed four mace and eight candareens; using them as ten-cash yielded a profit of five mace and four candareens.
translations.idiomatic: Standard cash weighed 1.2 mace; large coins weighed 4.8 mace—using them as ten-cash yielded 5.4 mace profit.

sentences.zh: 今以十當一，是反以四錢八分銅作一錢二分用也。

translations.literal: Now taking ten for one is inverting matters—using four mace and eight candareens of copper as one mace and two candareens.
translations.idiomatic: Now ten-for-one exchange means 4.8 mace of copper does the work of 1.2 mace.

sentences.zh: 民間私鎔改鑄，百弊叢生。

translations.literal: Private melting and recasting among the people produced a hundred abuses.
translations.idiomatic: Private melting and recasting bred countless abuses.

sentences.zh: 今天下皆用制錢，獨京師一隅用大錢，事不畫一。

translations.literal: Today all under Heaven uses standard cash; only the capital corner uses large coins—affairs are not uniform.
translations.idiomatic: The empire uses standard cash, but Beijing alone still uses large coins—a harmful inconsistency.

sentences.zh: 請悉復舊規，俾小民易於得食，盜源亦以稍弭。」

translations.literal: I request that everything be restored to the old regulations, so that the common people may easily obtain food, and the source of banditry may also be somewhat checked."
translations.idiomatic: He asked that old regulations be restored so common people could afford food and the roots of disorder somewhat checked."

sentences.zh: 十年，疏言軍事，略謂：「數年以來，地方軍事所謂失守，無所為守也，但聽其失。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he memorialized on military affairs, saying in summary: "In recent years what local military affairs call 'lost defense' is in fact defense that does nothing—merely letting it be lost.
translations.idiomatic: In 1860 he memorialized on military affairs: local 'defeats' were defenses that did nothing but watch places fall.

sentences.zh: 即坐以罪，僅革職留營而已。

translations.literal: Even when punished for it, they are only dismissed from office and kept in camp.
translations.idiomatic: Punishment meant only dismissal while remaining in camp.

sentences.zh: 所謂收復，不見其收，自然而复。

translations.literal: What is called 'recovery' shows no recovery; it recovers naturally.
translations.idiomatic: So-called 'recoveries' were not recoveries at all—places fell back when rebels left.

sentences.zh: 俟賊自去，即虛報克捷，上狀列保，以樹植私人。

translations.literal: When the bandits leave of themselves, false reports of victory are submitted upward and lists are filed for promotion, to plant private clients.
translations.idiomatic: When rebels withdrew, commanders filed false victory reports and promoted their own clients.

sentences.zh: 似此用兵，安有成功之一日？

translations.literal: With such use of troops, how can there be a day of success?
translations.idiomatic: With such warfare, how could success ever come?

sentences.zh: 臣愚以為今雖敗裂，機尚可轉。

translations.literal: Your servant foolishly believes that though the situation is now shattered, the opportunity can still be turned.
translations.idiomatic: Yet I believe that even now the tide can still be turned.

sentences.zh: 賊窺蘇、常久，一旦得之，子女玉帛，其意已饜，不特金陵老賊全股爭趨，即天長、六合之賊，亦涎其利。

translations.literal: The bandits have long coveted Suzhou and Changzhou; once they obtain them, with women, children, jade, and silks their desires are already sated; not only will the old bandits of Jinling all strive to go, but even the bandits of Tianchang and Luhe also covet the profit.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels had long coveted Suzhou and Changzhou; once they took those rich cities, veterans from Nanjing and bands from Tianchang and Luhe would all rush in.

sentences.zh: 宜乘彼勢方散緩，請特選重臣駐清、淮要地，統籌全局。

translations.literal: One should take advantage of their forces just dispersing and slackening; I request that a specially selected senior minister be stationed at the vital point of Qing and Huai to coordinate the overall situation.
translations.idiomatic: While their forces were still scattered and slack, he proposed stationing a senior minister on the Qing-Huai line to coordinate the whole theater.

sentences.zh: 頃諭旨令曾國籓赴兩江署任，規復甦、常，自寧國進兵，前後受敵，非萬全之計。

translations.literal: Recently an edict ordered Zeng Guofan to go to the two Jiangs as acting governor to plan recovery of Suzhou and Changzhou, advancing from Ningguo so as to be attacked front and rear—not a plan of complete security.
translations.idiomatic: A recent edict sending Zeng Guofan to the two Jiangs to recover Suzhou and Changzhou by advancing from Ningguo would expose him to attack from two sides—not a safe plan.

sentences.zh: 莫如令胡林翼自江北進攻，牽制安慶；

translations.literal: It would be better to order Hu Linyi to advance from north of the river and pin down Anqing;
translations.idiomatic: Better to have Hu Linyi advance from the north bank and pin down Anqing;

sentences.zh: 令楊載福以水師直下大江，互相策應；

translations.literal: order Yang Zaifu to lead the naval forces straight down the Great River, mutually supporting each other;
translations.idiomatic: have Yang Zaifu drive the fleet down the Yangzi in coordination;

sentences.zh: 令李若珠力攻天長、六合，以出江浦，遙立聲援。

translations.literal: order Li Ruozhu to press the attack on Tianchang and Luhe, emerging at Jiangpu to establish distant support;
translations.idiomatic: and Li Ruozhu press Tianchang and Luhe and threaten Jiangpu from afar;

sentences.zh: 密飭國籓潛引銳兵，倍道以取金陵，方為上策。

translations.literal: secretly order Guofan to lead picked troops by forced marches to take Jinling—that would be the superior strategy.
translations.idiomatic: while Zeng Guofan secretly led elite troops by forced march to take Nanjing—that would be the true strategy.

sentences.zh: 今日勞師糜餉，勢無窮已，兼各路統帥散而無紀，其賢者往往深入援絕，血戰殞身；

translations.literal: Today the army labors and funds are squandered, the momentum endlessly continuing; moreover commanders on every route are scattered without discipline, and the worthy often penetrate deep with relief cut off and die in bloody battle;
translations.idiomatic: Today armies exhaust the treasury without end; commanders act without coordination, and the brave often fight to the death with no support;

sentences.zh: 其不肖者坐擁厚兵，遇敵輒避；

translations.literal: The unworthy ones sit holding thick armies, and at encountering the enemy always flee;
translations.idiomatic: The unworthy commanders hoard large forces yet flee at the first sign of the enemy;

sentences.zh: 必得重臣領兵統馭，積弊既除，精神乃奮，此轉移之機也。」

translations.literal: One must obtain a senior minister to lead troops and command control; once accumulated abuses are removed, spirit then surges—this is the moment of turning the tide."
translations.idiomatic: Only if a senior minister takes command can entrenched corruption be cleared and morale revived—that is the key to changing the situation."

sentences.zh: 尋署戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was appointed acting Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed acting Vice Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 時各直省行團練，分遣大臣督辦，希祖疏言：「團者一時可集，練非經久不能。

translations.literal: At that time every province practiced local militia drilling; ministers were dispatched to supervise, and Xizu memorialized, saying: "Gathering a militia can be done in a moment, but training cannot be accomplished without long time.
translations.idiomatic: When every province raised local militias under dispatched ministers, Xizu memorialized: "A militia can be assembled quickly, but proper training takes sustained effort.

sentences.zh: 即云團練，非五六千人不可。

translations.literal: Even to speak of trained militia, no fewer than five or six thousand men are required.
translations.idiomatic: Even the minimum for militia training requires five or six thousand men.

sentences.zh: 計口授食，費已不貲。

translations.literal: Counting mouths and issuing rations, the expense is already incalculable.
translations.idiomatic: Feeding that many men would cost an enormous sum.

sentences.zh: 即使練成，而此五六千人制敵不足，騷動有餘，坐食貲詘，終虞譁潰。

translations.literal: Even if they are trained, yet these five or six thousand men are insufficient to control the enemy and more than enough to cause disturbance; sitting and eating they drain funds, and in the end one fears they will riot and break up.
translations.idiomatic: Even if trained, five or six thousand men would be too weak to fight effectively yet strong enough to cause trouble—they would consume funds idly and might eventually riot and scatter.

sentences.zh: 且遴往大臣，萬一與有司齟《齒吾》，必至互為水火，轉貽大局之憂。

translations.literal: Moreover, the selected ministers dispatched—if by any chance they clash with local officials, it will necessarily become mutual fire and water, in turn causing worry to the overall situation.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, if dispatched ministers clash with local officials, they will become bitter enemies and create grave problems for the overall situation.

sentences.zh: 請頒明諭，使知團練乃以自衛鄉閭，並不以此科斂，亦不必日給口糧，坐守困耗。

translations.literal: I request that a clear edict be issued so that people know militia training is for self-defense of villages and neighborhoods, and is not a basis for levying taxes, nor need there be daily issue of rations, sitting and guarding in exhausting depletion.
translations.idiomatic: Please issue a clear edict stating that militia drilling is for local self-defense only—not for tax levies or daily rations while men sit idle and drain resources.

sentences.zh: 否則用多費溢，正供無可挹注，不得不取諸民。

translations.literal: Otherwise with many used and expenses overflowing, regular revenue has nowhere from which to draw, and one cannot but take from the people.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise costs would spiral, regular revenue would be insufficient, and the burden would fall on the people.

sentences.zh: 輕則聚眾，重則返戈，大可慮也。」

translations.literal: In a light case they gather in crowds; in a serious case they turn their spears back—greatly to be feared."
translations.idiomatic: At best they would gather in mobs; at worst they would turn their weapons against the government—a serious danger."

sentences.zh: 英、法、俄、美四國合軍內犯，天津不守，希祖請暫就和議，遷延旬日，俾部署得以周詳。

translations.literal: Britain, France, Russia, and the United States combined their armies and invaded inland; Tianjin fell; Xizu requested temporarily accepting peace talks, delaying for ten days so that deployment could be thorough.
translations.idiomatic: When the allied armies of Britain, France, Russia, and the United States invaded and Tianjin fell, Xizu urged a temporary truce of ten days to allow time for thorough preparations.

sentences.zh: 僧格林沁獲英官巴夏裡，希祖疏請殺之。

translations.literal: Sengge Rinchen captured the British official Parkes; Xizu memorialized requesting his execution.
translations.idiomatic: After Sengge Rinchen captured the British official Harry Parkes, Xizu memorialized urging his execution.

sentences.zh: 未幾，敵軍深入，上巡幸熱河。

translations.literal: Before long the enemy army penetrated deep; the emperor toured to Rehe.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the enemy advanced deep into the country, and the emperor fled to Rehe.

sentences.zh: 希祖屢疏諫，不報，屢北望痛哭，遂得疾。

translations.literal: Xizu repeatedly memorialized in remonstrance, received no reply, repeatedly looked north and wept bitterly, and thus fell ill.
translations.idiomatic: Xizu remonstrated repeatedly without reply, often gazing north in tears until he fell ill.

sentences.zh: 已而和議成，兼署兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: Before long peace talks were concluded, and he was concurrently appointed acting Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: When peace was concluded, he was also appointed acting Vice Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 尋卒。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon after.

sentences.zh: =文瑞=文瑞，字叔安，烏蘇氏，滿洲鑲紅旗人。

translations.literal: Wen Rui, courtesy name Shuan, of the Usu clan, a Manchu of the Bordered Red Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Rui, courtesy name Shuan, of the Usu clan, was a Manchu of the Bordered Red Banner.

sentences.zh: 道光二十一年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year of Daoguang he passed the jinshi examination, was selected as a hanlin bachelor, and was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He became a jinshi in 1841, entered the Hanlin Academy, and was appointed a compiler.

sentences.zh: 擢侍講，五遷至左副都御史。

translations.literal: He was promoted to expositor, and after five promotions reached Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through five promotions from expositor to Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 文宗即位求言，文瑞疏陳四事，請選賢才，明賞罰，廣聽納，謹調攝，並錄乾隆元年左都御史孫家淦三習一弊疏以進，上嘉之。

translations.literal: When the Xianfeng Emperor ascended and sought advice, Wen Rui memorialized on four matters, requesting selection of worthy talent, clarity in rewards and punishments, broad acceptance of counsel, and careful self-restraint; he also transcribed and submitted the memorial of Left Censor-in-Chief Sun Jiagan in the first year of Qianlong on three habits and one abuse, and the emperor praised it.
translations.idiomatic: When the Xianfeng Emperor ascended the throne and sought advice, Wen Rui proposed four reforms—selecting talent, clarifying rewards and punishments, welcoming counsel, and careful governance—and submitted Sun Jiagan's famous "Three Habits and One Abuse" memorial from 1736, which the emperor commended.

sentences.zh: 咸豐三年，粵匪陷武昌東下，疏請於上海、鎮江僱用廣東紅單船，擇員統帶，以防江面；

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianfeng, the Cantonese rebels took Wuchang and marched east; he memorialized requesting hiring Guangdong red-flag ships at Shanghai and Zhenjiang, selecting officers to command them, to defend the river surface;
translations.idiomatic: In 1853, after rebels took Wuchang and marched east, he proposed hiring Guangdong red-flag ships at Shanghai and Zhenjiang under chosen commanders to defend the waterways;

sentences.zh: 並密察京師流言，以消逆萌、靖畿輔。

translations.literal: and also secretly investigated rumors in the capital, to extinguish rebellious impulses and pacify the metropolitan region.
translations.idiomatic: and also proposed monitoring capital rumors to suppress subversive sentiment and stabilize the metropolitan region.

sentences.zh: 上命諸大臣集議增兵籌餉，文瑞疏言：「兵餉為國家大政，遵旨會議，乃大學士等絕無一語及公，言笑晏晏，不知內閣何地，不詢會議何事。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered grand ministers to meet and discuss increasing troops and raising funds; Wen Rui memorialized, saying: "Military funds are a great state policy; following the edict to confer, yet the grand secretaries and others had not a single word touching the public good, talking and laughing at ease, not knowing where the Grand Secretariat was or what the conference was about.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor ordered ministers to discuss troop increases and military funding, Wen Rui protested: "Military finance is a matter of national importance, yet at the ordered conference the grand secretaries said nothing about the public interest—chatting casually as if unaware they were in the Grand Secretariat or what they had been called to discuss.

sentences.zh: 臣臚舉搘持之策，尚書孫瑞珍竟閒辭支吾，自述家私，形同市井。

translations.literal: Your servant enumerated policies to sustain the state, yet Minister Sun Ruizhen used idle words to evade, speaking of his private family affairs, like a marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: When I proposed ways to sustain the government, Minister Sun Ruizhen evaded with idle talk about private family matters, behaving like a common tradesman.

sentences.zh: 大臣如此，深堪悼嘆。」

translations.literal: Grand ministers such as this—deeply to be mourned and lamented."
translations.idiomatic: For senior ministers to behave this way is deeply lamentable."

sentences.zh: 又言：「二月朔為領俸定期，戶部款絀，早應籌畫。
