translations.literal: He also said: "The first of the second month is the fixed date for receiving salaries; the Ministry of Revenue's funds are short and should have been planned early.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote: "The first of the second month is payday, and the Ministry of Revenue's shortfall should have been addressed well in advance.

sentences.zh: 乃於是日清​​晨請旨，冀以停俸上諉朝廷。

translations.literal: Yet on that day at early dawn they requested instructions, hoping to shift blame for halting salaries onto the court.
translations.idiomatic: Instead they waited until payday morning to seek instructions, hoping to blame the court for any salary suspension.

sentences.zh: 又議行鈔法，並徵鋪稅，商民驚懼。

translations.literal: They also discussed implementing paper currency and levying shop taxes, and merchants and commoners were alarmed and fearful.
translations.idiomatic: They also proposed paper currency and shop taxes, alarming merchants and the public.

sentences.zh: 請發帑三十萬支放春俸，暫可流通，俾商民安業，鈔法鋪稅，暫從緩議。」

translations.literal: I request disbursing three hundred thousand taels from the treasury to pay spring salaries; this would temporarily restore circulation, enabling merchants and commoners to secure their livelihoods; paper currency and shop taxes should temporarily be deferred for discussion."
translations.idiomatic: I urge disbursing three hundred thousand taels for spring salaries to restore circulation and calm merchants and the public, while deferring paper currency and shop taxes."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: This was followed.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 又疏言：「鈔法之弊，放多收少，半為廢紙。

translations.literal: He also memorialized, saying: "The abuse of paper currency: when more is issued and less is accepted, half becomes waste paper.
translations.idiomatic: He also explained: "Paper currency fails when more is issued than accepted, reducing much of it to worthless paper.

sentences.zh: 放少收多，民間鈔無從得。

translations.literal: When less is issued and more is accepted, commoners have no way to obtain notes.
translations.idiomatic: When less is issued than accepted, the public cannot obtain notes at all.

sentences.zh: 若收放必均，是與之甲而取之乙，徒擾無益，非易銀鈔為錢票不可。

translations.literal: If receipt and issue must be equal, that is giving to A and taking from B—merely disturbing without benefit; only by changing silver notes to cash vouchers will it work.
translations.idiomatic: Requiring equal receipt and issue only takes from one group to give to another, causing disruption without benefit; silver notes must be replaced with cash vouchers.

sentences.zh: 擬就道光年間所設官號錢鋪五處，分儲戶、工兩局卯錢。

translations.literal: It is proposed to use the five government cash shops established in the Daoguang period, dividing and storing monthly cash from the Revenue and Works bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed using five government cash shops established under Daoguang, storing monthly coin reserves from the Revenue and Works bureaus.

sentences.zh: 京師俸餉，照公費發票之案，按數支給，以錢代銀。」

translations.literal: Salaries in the capital, following the precedent of public-expense invoice issuance, should be paid by number, using cash in place of silver."
translations.idiomatic: Capital salaries should be paid in cash rather than silver, following the precedent for public expense vouchers."

sentences.zh: 並具條目六事。

translations.literal: He also submitted six detailed articles.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted six detailed proposals.

sentences.zh: 疏入，議行。

translations.literal: The memorial entered and was adopted for implementation.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was submitted and adopted.

sentences.zh: 尋兼署大理寺卿，以天變奏請修省，上嘉納之。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was concurrently appointed acting Chief Judge of the Court of Judicial Review; on account of a celestial anomaly he memorialized requesting self-examination and reform, and the emperor praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed acting Chief Judge of the Court of Judicial Review and, citing a celestial anomaly, urged the court to examine itself, which the emperor commended.

sentences.zh: 刑部罪人劉秋貴死於獄，文瑞奏：「秋貴無病，一夕而死。

translations.literal: In the Ministry of Justice the convict Liu Qiugui died in prison; Wen Rui memorialized: "Qiugui had no illness and died in one night.
translations.idiomatic: When convict Liu Qiugui died in prison, Wen Rui reported: "Qiugui had no illness but died overnight.

sentences.zh: 刑部後四日入奏，改易日期，塗飾操縱，請嚴飭根究。」

translations.literal: The Ministry of Justice reported four days later, altering the date and embellishing and manipulating the account; I request strict orders to investigate to the root."
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Justice reported four days later with altered dates—please order a strict investigation of this cover-up."

sentences.zh: 山西崞縣民婦王劉氏拒姦死，罪人從輕比，刑部題駮，文瑞復奏：「原擬知州失出，請飭山西巡撫嚴劾。」

translations.literal: In Guo County, Shanxi, the commoner woman Wang Liushi died resisting rape; the convicted man was leniently sentenced; the Ministry of Justice submitted for rejection; Wen Rui again memorialized: "In the original sentence the prefect erred in leniency; I request ordering the Shanxi governor to investigate strictly."
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Liushi of Guo County, Shanxi, died resisting rape and the assailant received a lenient sentence, Wen Rui urged strict investigation of the prefect who had been too lenient."

sentences.zh: 上並從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed both proposals.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved both proposals.

sentences.zh: 粵匪入山西境，陷平陽等處，文瑞奏請飭督兵大臣嚴防入直隸要路。

translations.literal: The Cantonese rebels entered Shanxi territory and took Pingyang and other places; Wen Rui memorialized requesting orders to the supervising military ministers to strictly guard the vital routes into Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: When rebels entered Shanxi and captured Pingyang, Wen Rui urged military supervisors to block their advance into Zhili.

sentences.zh: 尋自臨洺關竄逼天津，命文瑞率兵駐通州。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward they fled from Linming Pass toward Tianjin; Wen Rui was ordered to lead troops stationed at Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When rebels broke toward Tianjin from Linming Pass, Wen Rui was ordered to garrison Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 奏言：「通州城垣樓櫓損壞，請集款建复。」

translations.literal: He memorialized, saying: "The walls and watchtowers of Tongzhou are damaged; I request gathering funds to rebuild and restore them."
translations.idiomatic: He reported: "Tongzhou's walls and towers are damaged; please allocate funds for repairs."

sentences.zh: 諭：「此守土之責，統兵大臣不必兼轄。」

translations.literal: An edict stated: "This is the responsibility of the territorial officials; the commander-in-chief need not additionally oversee it."
translations.idiomatic: The court replied: "That is the local officials' responsibility; the commanding general need not take it on."

sentences.zh: 擢刑部右侍郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Right Vice Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Right Vice Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 四年，以病乞罷。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, on account of illness he requested retirement.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he retired due to illness.

sentences.zh: 先是文瑞偕克勤郡王慶惠請捐銅鑄四項大錢濟兵餉，上從其請。

translations.literal: Earlier Wen Rui together with Prince Keqin Qinghui had requested donating copper to cast four kinds of large coins to relieve military funds, and the emperor followed their request.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Wen Rui and Prince Keqin Qinghui had proposed casting four denominations of large copper coins to fund the military, and the emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 及還京，病痊，命仍與慶惠董其事，設局開爐。

translations.literal: When he returned to the capital and his illness healed, he was ordered still to supervise the matter with Qinghui, establishing a bureau and opening furnaces.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned to Beijing recovered, he was ordered to continue supervising the project with Qinghui and establish minting operations.

sentences.zh: 上命尚書阿靈阿、御史范承典往銅廠查驗，文瑞奏劾阿靈阿等擅開爐房，恐有偷漏，上斥其負氣任性，降二級調用。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Minister A Ling'a and Censor Fan Chengdian to go to the copper works to inspect; Wen Rui memorialized impeaching A Ling'a and others for opening furnaces on their own authority, fearing there was evasion and leakage; the emperor rebuked him for arrogance and willfulness and demoted him two ranks for reassignment.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor sent Minister A Ling'a and Censor Fan Chengdian to inspect the copper works, Wen Rui impeached them for unauthorized smelting; the emperor rebuked his arrogance and demoted him two ranks.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，卒。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 1862.

sentences.zh: =毓祿=毓祿，字曉山，舒穆魯氏，滿洲正白旗人。

translations.literal: Yu Lu, courtesy name Xiaoshan, of the Shumulu clan, a Manchu of the Plain White Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Lu, courtesy name Xiaoshan, of the Shumulu clan, was a Manchu of the Plain White Banner.

sentences.zh: 道光二十一年進士，授刑部主事。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year of Daoguang he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed a chief clerk in the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He became a jinshi in 1841 and was appointed a chief clerk in the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 累升郎中，遷御史。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to director and transferred to censor.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to director and then censor.

sentences.zh: 軍興，安徽、江蘇、山東諸省皆暫停秋審。

translations.literal: With the raising of armies, Anhui, Jiangsu, Shandong, and other provinces all temporarily suspended autumn assizes.
translations.idiomatic: With the outbreak of war, Anhui, Jiangsu, Shandong, and other provinces suspended autumn assizes.

sentences.zh: 毓祿奏言：「寇踪所至，每先釋獄囚，脫其死而置之生，自必原為賊用。

translations.literal: Yu Lu memorialized, saying: "Wherever bandit tracks reach, they first release prison convicts; releasing them from death and placing them in life, they will naturally rejoin the rebels for use.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Lu wrote: "Wherever rebels go, they first release prisoners—freed from death, these men naturally join the enemy.

sentences.zh: 雖有投首減罪之例，而愚頑類多不知大義。

translations.literal: Although there are precedents for surrendering and reducing punishment, most of the foolish and stubborn do not know the greater moral principle.
translations.idiomatic: Although surrender can reduce punishment, most common criminals lack moral understanding.

sentences.zh: 聞直隸近因賊擾，將秋審諸囚，酌覈情罪，其謀、故、兇、盜、拒捕、殺人重囚，立即正法。

translations.literal: I hear that recently in Zhili, because of bandit disturbance, for autumn assize prisoners they carefully assessed circumstances and crimes; those convicted of plotting, intentional homicide, robbery, theft, resisting arrest, and murder as serious convicts were immediately executed according to law.
translations.idiomatic: I hear Zhili recently reviewed autumn-assize prisoners under rebel pressure: serious offenders in plotting, murder, robbery, and resisting arrest were executed immediately.

sentences.zh: 其情有可矜及例應緩決諸囚，即予減等發配，誠為權宜變通之道。

translations.literal: Those whose circumstances were pitiable and those whose cases called for deferred execution by precedent were immediately given reduced sentences and sent into exile—truly a flexible expedient measure.
translations.idiomatic: Prisoners whose cases warranted mercy or deferred execution were reduced in rank and exiled—an appropriate expedient.

sentences.zh: 現有軍務省分，應令一體遵辦。」

translations.literal: Existing provinces with military affairs should all be ordered to follow the same practice."
translations.idiomatic: All war-affected provinces should follow this practice."

sentences.zh: 京師行用大錢，當百、當五十二種壅滯不行，毓祿疏請商民應納旗租、地丁、關稅，於例定收鈔五成數內專收當百、當五十大錢二成，部收捐項應交錢票，亦一律納大錢。

translations.literal: In the capital large coins were in use; the hundred-cash and fifty-cash denominations were stagnant and not circulating; Yu Lu memorialized requesting that for merchants and commoners paying banner rents, land tax, and customs duties, within the statutory fifty percent acceptance of notes, twenty percent be collected exclusively in hundred-cash and fifty-cash large coins; for ministry receipt of donation items payable in cash vouchers, large coins should likewise uniformly be accepted.
translations.idiomatic: When hundred- and fifty-cash large coins stagnated in Beijing, Yu Lu proposed accepting them for twenty percent of merchant payments for rents, land tax, and customs within the statutory fifty-percent note quota, and for ministry donations as well.

sentences.zh: 七年，擢工科給事中，歷內閣侍讀學士、太僕寺少卿、通政司副使、內閣學士。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was promoted to Supervising Secretary of the Ministry of Works; he passed through Associate Reader of the Grand Secretariat, Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud, Vice Commissioner of the Office of Transmission, and Grand Secretariat Academician.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he became Supervising Secretary of Works and subsequently served as Associate Reader, Vice Minister of the Imperial Stud, Vice Commissioner of Transmission, and Grand Secretariat Academician.

sentences.zh: 同治三年，擢工部侍郎，兼管錢法堂。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tongzhi he was promoted to Vice Minister of Works and concurrently managed the Bureau of Currency.
translations.idiomatic: In 1864 he became Vice Minister of Works and concurrently oversaw the Bureau of Currency.

sentences.zh: 五年，奏言：「寶源局鑄當十錢，向系滇省解銅，以銅七鉛三配鑄。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he memorialized, saying: "The Baoyuan Bureau casts ten-cash coins; formerly copper was supplied from Yunnan, cast in a mixture of seven parts copper and three parts lead.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he reported: "The Baoyuan Bureau mints ten-cash coins from Yunnan copper in a seven-to-three copper-lead ratio.

sentences.zh: 近因滇銅久未解局，市銅低雜，致錢文輕小，例定每錢應重三錢二分。

translations.literal: Recently because Yunnan copper has long not reached the bureau, market copper is inferior and mixed, causing the coin characters to be light and small; by regulation each coin should weigh three mace and two candareens.
translations.idiomatic: Recently, with no Yunnan copper arriving, inferior market copper has made coins too light; each should weigh 3.2 mace.

sentences.zh: 請每屆收錢，以三錢為率，不及者即飭改鑄。」

translations.literal: I request that at each periodic coin collection, three mace be taken as the standard; those falling short should immediately be ordered to be recast."
translations.idiomatic: I urge that each coin-collection period enforce a minimum weight of three mace, with substandard coins ordered recast."

sentences.zh: 上斥寶泉、寶源二局不職之兩侍郎監督，並下吏議。

translations.literal: The emperor rebuked the two incompetent supervising vice ministers of the Baoquan and Baoyuan bureaus and referred them to the Ministry for disciplinary review.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rebuked the incompetent supervisors of the Baoquan and Baoyuan mints and ordered disciplinary proceedings.

sentences.zh: =徐繼畬=徐繼畬，字松龕，山西五台人。

translations.literal: Xu Jishe, courtesy name Songkan, a native of Wutai in Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Jishe, courtesy name Songkan, came from Wutai in Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 進士，選庶吉士，授編修，遷御史。

translations.literal: Jinshi; selected as hanlin bachelor; appointed compiler; transferred to censor.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi, he entered the Hanlin Academy as a compiler and later became a censor.

sentences.zh: 迭疏劾忻州知州史夢蛟、保德知州林樹雲營求升遷，登州知府英文諱災催徵，榮河知縣武履中藉事科斂。

translations.literal: He repeatedly memorialized impeaching Xinzhou Prefect Shi Mengjiao and Baode Prefect Lin Shuyun for seeking promotion through improper means; Dengzhou Prefect Ying Wen for concealing disasters and pressing tax collection; and Ronghe Magistrate Wu Lüzhong for levying fees by exploiting matters.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly impeached Xinzhou Prefect Shi Mengjiao and Baode Prefect Lin Shuyun for seeking promotion through patronage, Dengzhou Prefect Ying Wen for concealing disasters to press tax collection, and Ronghe Magistrate Wu Lüzhong for exploiting official business to levy fees.

sentences.zh: 又疏請除大臣回護調停積習。

translations.literal: He also memorialized requesting the removal of grand ministers' accumulated habit of shielding and mediating.
translations.idiomatic: He also urged an end to the habit of senior ministers shielding one another through mediation.

sentences.zh: 又疏陳政體宜崇簡要，略謂：「皇上廣開言路，諸臣條奏苟有可取，無不通行訓諭，惟是積習疲玩已久，煌煌聖諭，漠不經意，輕褻甚矣。

translations.literal: He also memorialized stating that governmental form should honor simplicity and essentials, briefly saying: "Your Majesty has broadly opened the channel of advice; whenever ministers' memorials had merit, none failed to be issued as instructions throughout; yet the accumulated habit of lax neglect has long persisted—the brilliant imperial edicts are treated with indifference, treated lightly and disrespectfully to a great degree.
translations.idiomatic: He also argued that government should be simpler, writing: "Although the emperor welcomes memorials and issues edicts whenever proposals have merit, officials have long treated even solemn imperial decrees with indifference and disrespect.

sentences.zh: 臣以為諸臣條奏，或非大體所關，或非時務所急，原不必悉見明文。

translations.literal: Your servant believes that ministers' memorials may not touch the fundamental structure or may not be urgent to current affairs; originally not all need appear as explicit documents.
translations.idiomatic: I believe not every memorial touches fundamental policy or urgent affairs, and not all need formal written response.

sentences.zh: 若事關切要，聖慮折中，期於必行者，即降諭旨，宜重考成。

translations.literal: If the matter touches what is essential, and the imperial deliberation has weighed it with the expectation of mandatory execution, then when an edict is issued, strict accountability should be enforced.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor decides a matter must be carried out, the edict should come with strict accountability.

sentences.zh: 度其事之難易，限年興革。

translations.literal: Assessing the difficulty or ease of the matter, set a time limit in years for enactment or abolition.
translations.idiomatic: Set deadlines according to difficulty for implementation or reform.

sentences.zh: 如仍前玩視，於本案外重治以違旨之罪。

translations.literal: If they still treat it as before with neglect, beyond the original case severely punish them with the crime of disobeying the edict.
translations.idiomatic: Officials who continue to neglect such orders should face additional punishment for disobedience.

sentences.zh: 此教令之宜簡也。

translations.literal: This is how instructions and orders should be simplified.
translations.idiomatic: This is how imperial instructions should be simplified.

sentences.zh: 六部則例日增，律不足，求之例；

translations.literal: In the Six Ministries precedents increase daily; when the code is insufficient, one seeks precedents;
translations.idiomatic: The Six Ministries accumulate precedents daily—when the code is insufficient, officials turn to precedents;

sentences.zh: 例不足，求之案：陳陳相因，棼亂如絲。

translations.literal: when precedents are insufficient, one seeks cases: piled one upon another, tangled and confused as silk threads.
translations.idiomatic: when precedents fail, they turn to case records—layer upon layer until the tangle is like silk threads.

sentences.zh: 論者謂六部之權，全歸書吏。

translations.literal: Commentators say the power of the Six Ministries rests entirely with the clerks.
translations.idiomatic: Critics say the Six Ministries' real power lies entirely with clerks.

sentences.zh: 非書吏之有權，條例之煩多使然也。

translations.literal: It is not that the clerks have power—the profusion of regulations and precedents makes it so.
translations.idiomatic: This is not because clerks are powerful but because regulations have become too numerous.

sentences.zh: 臣以為當就現行事例，精審詳定，取切於事理者，事省十之五，文省十之七，名曰簡明事例，使當事各官得以知其梗概，庶不至聽命於書吏。

translations.literal: Your servant believes one should take existing precedents, examine and fix them carefully, select those suited to principle and circumstance, reduce matters by five-tenths and text by seven-tenths, and call them Simplified Essential Precedents, so that officials in charge may know the gist and not end up taking orders from clerks.
translations.idiomatic: I propose reviewing existing precedents, keeping only what is essential—cutting matters by half and text by seventy percent—into a "Simplified Essential Precedents" so officials need not rely on clerks.

sentences.zh: 此則例之宜簡也。

translations.literal: This is how precedents should be simplified.
translations.idiomatic: This is how precedents should be simplified.

sentences.zh: 考功、職方，議功議過，使百僚知勸懲也。

translations.literal: The Bureau of Personnel Evaluation and the Bureau of Appointments discuss merit and discuss faults, so that all officials know encouragement and punishment.
translations.idiomatic: The bureaus of personnel evaluation and appointments assess merit and fault so officials understand reward and punishment.

sentences.zh: 現行之條，苦於太繁太密，不得大體。

translations.literal: Present regulations suffer from being too numerous and too detailed, missing the fundamental structure.
translations.idiomatic: Current regulations are too numerous and detailed to serve their larger purpose.

sentences.zh: 嘗見各直省州縣有蒞任不及一年，而罰俸至數年十數年者，左牽右掣，動輒得咎。

translations.literal: One often sees in provinces that prefects and magistrates who have held office less than one year are fined salary for several or even more than ten years, pulled left and right, faulted at every move.
translations.idiomatic: I have seen officials in office less than a year fined several or even ten years' salary, tripped up at every turn.

sentences.zh: 且議處愈增愈密，規避亦愈出愈奇，彼此相遁，上下相詭，非所以清治道也。

translations.literal: Moreover, as disciplinary measures increase they grow ever more detailed, and evasion also becomes ever more ingenious; each side evades the other, upper and lower deceive each other—this is not the way to purify the path of governance.
translations.idiomatic: As disciplinary rules multiply, so do evasions—officials deceiving one another at every level—which does not clarify governance.

sentences.zh: 臣以為各官處分，凡關於國計民生，官箴品行，不妨從重從嚴；

translations.literal: Your servant believes that in officials' disciplinary measures, for all that touches state revenue and people's livelihood, official integrity and conduct, there is no harm in being heavy and strict;
translations.idiomatic: I believe punishments should remain strict for matters affecting public finance, people's livelihood, and official integrity;

sentences.zh: 其事涉細微，無關治體，與夫苛責太深，情勢所難者，當準情酌理，大加刪削。

translations.literal: for matters touching trifles, unrelated to the structure of governance, and for excessively harsh demands difficult under the circumstances, one should measure sentiment and weigh reason and greatly reduce and cut.
translations.idiomatic: but trivial matters, cases irrelevant to governance, and excessively harsh demands should be greatly reduced after weighing circumstances.

sentences.zh: 此處分之宜簡也。」

translations.literal: This is how disciplinary measures should be simplified."
translations.idiomatic: This is how disciplinary measures should be simplified."

sentences.zh: 疏入，上嘉納。

translations.literal: The memorial entered and the emperor praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor commended and accepted the memorial.

sentences.zh: 旋召入對，論時事至為流涕。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was summoned for audience; discussing current affairs he wept to an extreme degree.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon summoned for audience and wept while discussing current affairs.

sentences.zh: 十六年，出為廣西潯州知府，擢福建延邵道，調署汀漳龍道。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he went out as Prefect of Xunzhou in Guangxi; was promoted to Intendant of Yan-Shao in Fujian; and was transferred to acting Intendant of Ting-Zhang-Long Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he became Prefect of Xunzhou in Guangxi, was promoted to Intendant of Yan-Shao in Fujian, and served as acting Intendant of Ting-Zhang-Long Circuit.

sentences.zh: 海疆事起，敵艦聚廈門，與漳州隔一水，居民日數驚。

translations.literal: When coastal affairs erupted, enemy ships gathered at Xiamen, separated from Zhangzhou by one stretch of water; residents were alarmed daily.
translations.idiomatic: When hostilities erupted along the coast, enemy ships gathered at Xiamen across the water from Zhangzhou, alarming residents daily.

sentences.zh: 繼畬處以鎮定，民賴以安。

translations.literal: Jishe handled matters with calm steadiness, and the people relied on him for security.
translations.idiomatic: Jishe maintained calm, and the people found security in his leadership.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，遷兩廣鹽運使，旬日擢廣東按察使。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he was transferred to Salt Transport Commissioner of the Two Guangs; within ten days he was promoted to Surveillance Commissioner of Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year he became Salt Transport Commissioner of the Two Guangs and within ten days was promoted to Surveillance Commissioner of Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，遷福建布政使。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year he was transferred to provincial administration commissioner of Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year he became Provincial Administration Commissioner of Fujian.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，授廣西巡撫，未赴官，調福建。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he was appointed governor of Guangxi; before taking office he was transferred to Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year he was named Governor of Guangxi but was transferred to Fujian before taking up the post.

sentences.zh: 閩浙總督劉韻珂以病乞假，繼畬暫兼署總督。

translations.literal: Governor-General of Fujian and Zhejiang Liu Yunke requested leave on account of illness, and Jishe temporarily also acted as governor-general.
translations.idiomatic: When Governor-General Liu Yunke of Fujian and Zhejiang took sick leave, Jishe served temporarily as acting governor-general.

sentences.zh: 福州初通商，英吉利人僦居會城烏石山神光寺，士民大譁，言路以入告，上命韻珂、繼畬令其遷徙，久之乃移居道山觀。

translations.literal: When Fuzhou first opened to trade, Englishmen rented residence at the Shenguang Temple on Wushi Mountain in the provincial capital; gentry and commoners were greatly alarmed, and censorial channels reported it to the throne; the emperor ordered Yunke and Jishe to make them relocate, and only after a long time did they move to the Daoshan Daoist abbey.
translations.idiomatic: When Fuzhou first opened to foreign trade, Englishmen leased the Shenguang Temple on Wushi Mountain in the capital, provoking a public outcry that reached the throne. The emperor ordered Yunke and Jishe to have them relocated; only after considerable delay did they move to the Daoshan Daoist abbey.

sentences.zh: 士民以繼畬初不力拒，終不慊，言者屢論劾。

translations.literal: The gentry and commoners, because Jishe at first had not strongly resisted, were never satisfied; memorialists repeatedly impeached him.
translations.idiomatic: The local gentry and populace, resentful that Jishe had not resisted the foreigners forcefully enough, kept submitting impeachments against him.

sentences.zh: 繼畬初入覲，宣宗詢各國風土形勢，奏對甚悉，退遂編次為書曰瀛寰志略，未進呈而宣宗崩，言者抨擊及之。

translations.literal: When Jishe first entered the capital for audience, the Daoguang Emperor inquired about the customs and terrain of each country; his written and oral replies were very thorough; on retiring he arranged them into a book called Yinghuan Zhilue, but before he submitted it the Daoguang Emperor died, and memorialists attacked him over it.
translations.idiomatic: On his first audience with the Daoguang Emperor, Jishe answered thoroughly on the customs and geography of foreign nations. He later compiled his notes into Yinghuan Zhilue, but the emperor died before he could present it, and critics seized on the work to attack him.

sentences.zh: 繼畬父潤第，治陸王之學。

translations.literal: Jishe's father Run Di studied the learning of Lu-Wang.
translations.idiomatic: Jishe's father Run Di was a scholar of the Lu-Wang school of Neo-Confucianism.

sentences.zh: 繼畬承其教，務博覽，通時事。

translations.literal: Jishe inherited his teaching, striving for broad reading and mastery of current affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He carried on his father's learning, reading widely and keeping abreast of current affairs.

sentences.zh: 在閩、粵久，熟外情，務持重，以恩信約束。

translations.literal: Having long been in Fujian and Guangdong, he was familiar with foreign conditions; he strove for restraint and governed through kindness and good faith.
translations.idiomatic: Long service in Fujian and Guangdong gave him deep knowledge of foreign affairs; he governed with steady restraint, relying on kindness and credibility.

sentences.zh: 在官廉謹。

translations.literal: In office he was incorrupt and careful.
translations.idiomatic: He was incorrupt and conscientious in office.

sentences.zh: 罷歸，主平遙書院以自給。

translations.literal: Dismissed and returned home, he headed the Pingyao Academy to support himself.
translations.idiomatic: After leaving office he returned home and supported himself as head of the Pingyao Academy.

sentences.zh: 尋卒。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon afterward.

sentences.zh: =王發桂=王發桂，字笑山，直隸清苑人。

translations.literal: Wang Fagui, courtesy name Xiaoshan, was a native of Qingyuan in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Fagui, whose courtesy name was Xiaoshan, came from Qingyuan in Zhili Province.

sentences.zh: 道光十六年進士，授禮部主事，充軍機章京，累遷郎中。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of the Daoguang reign he passed the jinshi examination, was appointed a principal clerk in the Ministry of Rites, served as a secretarial clerk of the Grand Council, and was repeatedly promoted to bureau director.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of 1836, he became a principal clerk in the Ministry of Rites, served as a Grand Council secretarial clerk, and rose to bureau director.

sentences.zh: 咸豐三年，上疏言軍事，被嘉納。

translations.literal: In the third year of the Xianfeng reign he submitted a memorial on military affairs and was praised and accepted.
translations.idiomatic: In 1853 he memorialized on military affairs and received the emperor's approval.

sentences.zh: 尋遷御史。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was transferred to censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to censor.

sentences.zh: 洪秀全既踞江寧，分兵北犯，發桂疏言：「順德、正定地當衝要，請屯兵扼隘。」

translations.literal: After Hong Xiuquan had seized Jiangning and sent troops northward in invasion, Fagui memorialized: "Shunde and Zhengding occupy vital positions; I request that troops be stationed to hold the passes."
translations.idiomatic: After Hong Xiuquan seized Nanjing and sent armies north, Fagui urged that troops be posted at the strategic passes around Shunde and Zhengding."

sentences.zh: 併條列六事，曰：謹偵報，嚴催儹，慎查勘，明曉諭，廣撫卹，籌協濟。

translations.literal: He also listed six items in detail, namely: careful scouting and reporting, strict urging of transport, cautious investigation and surveying, clear instruction and announcement, broad relief and care, and planning mutual aid.
translations.idiomatic: He further set out six measures: careful intelligence work, strict logistics, thorough field inspection, clear public notice, expanded relief, and coordinated mutual aid.

sentences.zh: 又疏薦貴州道員胡林翼知兵能勝重任，請超擢，俾任軍旅，上命林翼留湖北襄軍事。

translations.literal: He again memorialized recommending the Guizhou circuit intendant Hu Linyi as knowing military affairs and able to bear heavy responsibility, requesting exceptional promotion and assignment to military command; the emperor ordered Linyi to remain in Hubei to assist in military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He also recommended Hu Linyi, circuit intendant of Guizhou, as a proven military man fit for high command and asked for his rapid promotion; the emperor ordered Hu to stay in Hubei to manage military affairs.

sentences.zh: 迭疏請令各省汰舊伍，練新兵，設鄉團，值有事則新軍進戰，鄉團設防，以明戚繼光紀效新書、練兵實紀訓練將士。

translations.literal: In repeated memorials he requested that each province weed out old troops, drill new armies, and establish local militia; when trouble arose the new armies would advance to fight and the militia would hold defenses, making clear the Ji Xiaoxin Shu and Lianbing Shiji of Qi Jiguang for training officers and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: In successive memorials he urged provinces to replace old troops with newly drilled armies and local militia—new armies for the field, militia for defense—following Qi Jiguang's military manuals for training.

sentences.zh: 賊渡河偪近畿輔，疏請蒐簡軍實，選精銳為後備，並蠲貧民房稅，撫流亡以安人心，下所司議行。

translations.literal: When the bandits crossed the river and pressed close to the capital region, he memorialized requesting inspection and sorting of military resources, selection of crack troops as reserves, and also exemption of poor households from house taxes and relief of displaced persons to settle popular hearts; the matter was referred to the responsible offices for deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: As rebels crossed the river and threatened the capital region, he asked for a review of military resources, selection of elite reserves, tax relief for the poor, and resettlement of refugees to calm public anxiety; the court referred the proposals for implementation.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「軍興以來，大臣獲罪，多以從軍自效，位崇性驕，不可任使，坐耗糧糈，無裨軍政。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "Since the rise of military mobilization, grand ministers who incurred guilt have mostly sought to redeem themselves through military service; high in rank and proud in temperament, they cannot be entrusted with duties, yet they idly consume provisions without benefiting military administration.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote: "Since the war began, disgraced senior officials have often sought redemption on campaign—too proud and too senior to be useful, yet still consuming rations without helping the war effort.

sentences.zh: 且主將曲庇，輒請起用，有罪幾同無罪，圖功適以冒功。

translations.literal: Moreover, commanders show favor and partiality, repeatedly requesting their reinstatement; guilt is nearly the same as innocence, and seeking merit becomes merely claiming merit.
translations.idiomatic: Commanders protect their favorites and push for their reinstatement, so punishment means little and claimed victories become false credit.

sentences.zh: 頃副都統達洪阿退縮失律，致知縣謝子澄、副都統佟鑑同時死寇。

translations.literal: Recently the vice commander-in-chief Da Hong'a retreated in violation of discipline, causing the magistrate Xie Zicheng and the vice commander-in-chief Tong Jian to die at the hands of bandits at the same time.
translations.idiomatic: Recently Vice Commander-in-Chief Da Hong'a broke discipline in retreat, leaving Magistrate Xie Zicheng and Vice Commander-in-Chief Tong Jian to die fighting the rebels.

sentences.zh: 欽差大臣勝保賜以神雀刀，原令便宜行事，乃自入直境，未戮一人；

translations.literal: The imperial commissioner Senggebao was granted the divine sparrow-hawk sword and originally empowered to act at discretion, yet from the time he entered the Zhili borders he has slain not a single man;
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Commissioner Senggebao was given the spirit-hawk sword and discretionary powers, yet since entering Zhili he had killed no enemy;

sentences.zh: 而於獲戾大臣，多所論薦，以私廢公，抑阻士氣。

translations.literal: yet toward guilty grand ministers he has made many recommendations, putting private favor above public duty and suppressing the spirit of officers.
translations.idiomatic: while repeatedly recommending disgraced officials for reuse, putting personal favor ahead of duty and dampening morale.

sentences.zh: 請按治達洪阿以下，行軍法。

translations.literal: I request that Da Hong'a and those below him be prosecuted according to military law.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that Da Hong'a and others be punished under military law.

sentences.zh: 紀律既嚴，軍威自振。」

translations.literal: Once discipline is strict, military prestige will naturally revive."
translations.idiomatic: Strict discipline, he argued, would restore the army's fighting spirit."

sentences.zh: 並被採納。

translations.literal: These points were all adopted.
translations.idiomatic: The court accepted these recommendations.

sentences.zh: 累遷給事中、鴻臚寺卿。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to supervising secretary and director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the posts of supervising secretary and director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 八年，复疏論時事，言：「宜上廉恥，重訓練，以求將帥之才。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he again memorialized discussing current affairs, saying: "One should exalt integrity and shame, emphasize training, so as to seek talent among generals and commanders.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he again addressed current affairs: "The court should cultivate integrity, emphasize training, and seek out real commanders.

sentences.zh: 李續賓、唐訓方起自末僚，能自張一軍，轉戰千里。

translations.literal: Li Xubin and Tang Xunfang rose from the lowest posts yet were able each to command an army independently and fight across a thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: Men like Li Xubin and Tang Xunfang rose from humble ranks to lead independent armies across vast distances.

sentences.zh: 敦樸廉潔，勇往任事之人，隨地而有，請飭督撫採訪奏聞。

translations.literal: Men of simple integrity, incorruptibility, and bold willingness to take responsibility exist everywhere; I request that governors-general and governors be ordered to seek them out and report them to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Honest, capable men willing to take responsibility can be found everywhere; he asked governors to seek them out and report them.

sentences.zh: 物力艱窘，莫甚於湖南；

translations.literal: Material resources are most strained in Hunan;
translations.idiomatic: No province was more strapped for resources than Hunan;

sentences.zh: 軍餉糜費，莫甚於江蘇。

translations.literal: military funds are most lavishly squandered in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: and none squandered military funds more than Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 自湖南得左宗棠，江蘇得王​​有齡，而餉源日裕。

translations.literal: Since Hunan obtained Zuo Zongtang and Jiangsu obtained Wang Youling, sources of funds have daily grown ample.
translations.idiomatic: Once Hunan had Zuo Zongtang and Jiangsu had Wang Youling, revenue recovered steadily.

sentences.zh: 夫興利莫如去★L2，今司計者日言捐餉，而鹽、漕、糧稅，凡國家自然之利，一任廢弛。

translations.literal: In promoting profit nothing is better than removing abuses; yet today those who manage revenue daily speak of contribution funds for provisions, while salt, grain transport, land tax, and every natural source of state revenue are allowed to fall into neglect.
translations.idiomatic: To increase revenue, nothing works better than removing abuses; yet officials talked only of soliciting contributions while letting salt, transport, and tax revenues—the state's natural income—lapse.

sentences.zh: 請下所司議整飭。

translations.literal: I request that the responsible offices be ordered to deliberate on restoration and regulation.
translations.idiomatic: He asked the relevant offices to deliberate on reforms.

sentences.zh: 兩廣總督黃宗漢赴粵，遷延六月，遲不之官。

translations.literal: Governor-General of the Two Guangs Huang Zonghan, having gone toward Guangdong, delayed for six months and was slow to take office.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Huang Zonghan delayed six months before taking up his post in Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 城淪於敵，巡撫柏貴莫知為計。

translations.literal: When the city fell to the enemy, Governor Bo Gui knew no plan.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell, Governor Bo Gui was at a loss.

sentences.zh: 城東居民殺敵數百，柏貴輒為懸賞緝殺人者。

translations.literal: Residents east of the city killed several hundred enemies, yet Bo Gui immediately offered rewards to hunt down the killers.
translations.idiomatic: When eastern residents killed hundreds of enemy soldiers, Bo Gui posted bounties for their arrest instead.

sentences.zh: 貴州巡撫蔣霨遠當叛苗、教匪日久鴟張，未聞有所措施。

translations.literal: Governor of Guizhou Jiang Yuyuan, facing long-raging Miao rebels and religious bandits, was never heard to have taken any measures.
translations.idiomatic: In Guizhou, Governor Jiang Yuyuan presided over prolonged Miao and sectarian rebellions without taking effective action.

sentences.zh: 此皆才力不逮，遂使一方塗炭。

translations.literal: All these were cases where talent and strength fell short, causing a whole region to be plunged into misery.
translations.idiomatic: Such failures of capacity had left whole regions in ruin.

sentences.zh: 聖主恩威並用，尤所仰望。」

translations.literal: The sage ruler's combined use of kindness and authority is what one especially looks to."
translations.idiomatic: He placed his hope in the emperor's balanced use of grace and force."

sentences.zh: 歷太僕寺卿、通政使、左副都御史。

translations.literal: He served successively as director of the Court of the Imperial Stud, commissioner of the Office of Transmission, and left vice censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: He held the posts of director of the Court of the Imperial Stud, transmission commissioner, and left vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 同治二年，署工部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the second year of the Tongzhi reign he served as acting vice minister of works.
translations.idiomatic: In 1863 he served as acting Vice Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 疏薦戶部郎中王正誼守潔才優，以忤肅順得罪，請復其官，報可。

translations.literal: He memorialized recommending Wang Zhengyi, a bureau director in the Ministry of Revenue, as incorrupt and talented; having offended Su Shun and been punished, he requested restoration of his office; approval was granted.
translations.idiomatic: He recommended Wang Zhengyi of the Ministry of Revenue—a man of integrity wrongly punished for opposing Su Shun—and the court restored him.

sentences.zh: 授禮部侍郎，調刑部，又調工部。

translations.literal: He was appointed vice minister of rites, transferred to the Ministry of Punishments, and again transferred to the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He became Vice Minister of Rites, then transferred to Punishments and later to Works.

sentences.zh: 五年，以疾乞免。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he requested dismissal on account of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In 1866 he asked to retire because of illness.

sentences.zh: 九年，卒。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 1870.

sentences.zh: =廉兆綸=廉兆綸，初名師敏，字葆醇，順天寧河人。

translations.literal: Lian Zhaolun, original name Shimmin, courtesy name Baochun, was a native of Ninghe in Shuntian.
translations.idiomatic: Lian Zhaolun, originally named Shimmin and courtesy name Baochun, came from Ninghe in Shuntian.

sentences.zh: 道光二十年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year of the Daoguang reign he passed the jinshi examination, was selected as a bachelor of the Hanlin Academy, and was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of 1840, he entered the Hanlin as a bachelor and became a compiler.

sentences.zh: 宣宗知其賢，將擢用，以父憂歸，遺命諸臣可大用者，兆綸與焉。

translations.literal: The Daoguang Emperor knew his worth and was about to promote him, but he returned home on account of his father's mourning; in the deathbed instructions listing ministers who could be greatly employed, Zhaolun was among them.
translations.idiomatic: The Daoguang Emperor had intended to promote him when he left for mourning; on his deathbed the emperor named Zhaolun among officials fit for high office.

sentences.zh: 咸豐元年，服除。

translations.literal: In the first year of the Xianfeng reign his mourning period ended.
translations.idiomatic: When the mourning period ended in 1851, he returned to service.

sentences.zh: 二年，大考二等。

translations.literal: In the second year he received second rank in the triennial examination.
translations.idiomatic: In 1852 he scored second rank in the triennial evaluation.

sentences.zh: 三年，直南書房。

translations.literal: In the third year he served in the Southern Library.
translations.idiomatic: In 1853 he served in the Southern Library.

sentences.zh: 四年，授右贊善，超擢翰林院侍講學士，督江西學政，轉侍讀學士，再擢內閣學士。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was appointed right tutor, was exceptionally promoted to expositor of the Hanlin Academy, supervised education in Jiangxi, was transferred to reader of the Hanlin Academy, and was again promoted to grand secretary of the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In 1854 he became right tutor, was rapidly promoted through Hanlin expositor and reader to grand secretary while serving as Jiangxi education commissioner.

sentences.zh: 五年，授工部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was appointed vice minister of works.
translations.idiomatic: In 1855 he became Vice Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 時粵匪石達開擾江西，侍郎曾國籓率師御之，寇張甚，陷州縣五十餘，逼會城。

translations.literal: At that time the Cantonese rebel Shi Dakai harassed Jiangxi; Vice Minister Zeng Guofan led troops to resist him; the bandits were very powerful, seizing more than fifty prefectures and districts and pressing upon the provincial capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Dakai's rebels overran Jiangxi, Zeng Guofan marched against them; the rebels seized more than fifty counties and threatened the provincial capital.

sentences.zh: 上命兆綸幫辦廣信、饒州防剿，兆綸奏言：「江西通省募勇計一萬五六千人，各不相統屬。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Zhaolun to assist in defense and suppression at Guangxin and Raozhou; Zhaolun memorialized: "In Jiangxi province as a whole, recruited braves total about fifteen or sixteen thousand men, each group not subordinate to the others.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor put Zhaolun in charge of defense at Guangxin and Raozhou; he reported that Jiangxi's fifteen or sixteen thousand militiamen answered to no unified command.

sentences.zh: 地方有警，勝則互訐以競功，敗則爭潰而不相救。

translations.literal: When the locality is alarmed, if victorious they mutually impeach one another to compete for credit; if defeated they scramble to flee and do not rescue one another.
translations.idiomatic: In action they competed for credit when winning and fled separately when losing, refusing to help one another.

sentences.zh: 甚且擾民冒餉，乘便營私，其弊不勝枚舉。

translations.literal: They even harass the people, falsely claim rations, and seize opportunities for private profit; the abuses are too numerous to list.
translations.idiomatic: They even extorted civilians, padded rations, and used the chaos for private gain—abuses too many to count.

sentences.zh: 今賊勢日張，瑞州、臨江相繼失守，設有倉卒，以此散而無紀者當之，何恃不恐？

translations.literal: Now the bandit power grows daily; Ruizhou and Linjiang fell in succession; should there be a sudden emergency, with these scattered and undisciplined men to meet it, on what would one rely without fear?
translations.idiomatic: With rebels growing stronger and Ruizhou and Linjiang already fallen, how could scattered, undisciplined troops meet a sudden crisis?

sentences.zh: 惟有將所募之勇，裁去一切名號，並為三四軍，每軍得四五千人，統以監司方面素有威望者，庶可責成功。」

translations.literal: There is nothing for it but to cut away all titles from the recruited braves, combine them into three or four armies of four or five thousand men each, and place them under circuit intendants and regional officials of long-standing prestige, so that success may be demanded of them."
translations.idiomatic: He proposed merging the militia into three or four armies of four to five thousand men each under respected provincial officials who could be held accountable."

sentences.zh: 六年三月，兆綸按試廣信，賊陷吉安、撫州，進據安仁，兆綸上疏請援，並以練勇千守貴溪。

translations.literal: In the third month of the sixth year Zhaolun conducted examinations at Guangxin; the bandits seized Ji'an and Fuzhou and advanced to occupy Anren; Zhaolun submitted a memorial requesting reinforcements and also posted a thousand drilled braves to guard Guixi.
translations.idiomatic: In March 1856, while examining candidates at Guangxin, he learned that rebels had taken Ji'an and Fuzhou and occupied Anren; he asked for reinforcements and posted a thousand militiamen at Guixi.

sentences.zh: 賊竄德興，陷建昌，廣信勢益孤，兆綸督諸生集鄉團，與廣信知府沈葆楨、上饒知縣楊昇籌防禦。

translations.literal: The bandits fled to Dexing and seized Jianchang; Guangxin's position grew ever more isolated; Zhaolun directed students to gather local militia and, together with Guangxin Prefect Shen Baozhen and Shangrao Magistrate Yang Sheng, planned defense.
translations.idiomatic: As rebels raided Dexing and took Jianchang, leaving Guangxin isolated, Zhaolun rallied students into militia and coordinated defenses with Shen Baozhen and Magistrate Yang Sheng.

sentences.zh: 遣上饒諸生郭守謙率鄉勇三百夜襲金谿，諸生曾守誠奮勇先入城，賊不虞兵至，奪西南門逸，克其城。

translations.literal: He sent the Shangrao student Guo Shouqian to lead three hundred local braves in a night attack on Jinxi; the student Zeng Shoucheng bravely entered the city first; the bandits did not expect troops to arrive, fled through the southwest gate, and the city was taken.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Guo Shouqian with three hundred militiamen on a night raid on Jinxi; Zeng Shoucheng broke in first, and the surprised rebels fled through the southwest gate as the city fell.

sentences.zh: 乘勝會攻建昌，而饒州又陷，官軍敗績，廣信益危。

translations.literal: Following up the victory they joined in attacking Jianchang, but Raozhou fell again, the government armies suffered defeat, and Guangxin grew still more perilous.
translations.idiomatic: Pressing the advantage against Jianchang, they learned Raozhou had fallen and government forces had been routed, leaving Guangxin in graver danger.

sentences.zh: 兆綸與國籓等合疏請截留閩兵一千六百專攻建昌，分檄守謙與在籍道員石景芬防剿。

translations.literal: Zhaolun together with Guofan and others jointly memorialized requesting that sixteen hundred Fujian troops be detained and dedicated to attacking Jianchang, and dispatched orders to Shouqian and the resident circuit intendant Shi Jingfen for defense and suppression.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaolun and Zeng Guofan jointly asked that 1,600 Fujian troops be kept to retake Jianchang and ordered Shouqian and resident official Shi Jingfen to carry on defense.

sentences.zh: 六月，國籓遣都司畢金科复饒州，兆綸飭景芬、守謙等馳攻撫州。

translations.literal: In the sixth month Guofan sent Director Bi Jinke to recover Raozhou; Zhaolun ordered Jingfen, Shouqian, and others to rush to attack Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Zeng Guofan sent Bi Jinke to retake Raozhou while Zhaolun ordered Jingfen and Shouqian to strike at Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 會賊連陷廣昌、南豐、新城、瀘溪四縣，八月，守謙軍撫州張家橋，三接皆捷，窮追遇伏，力戰死。

translations.literal: Just then the bandits in succession seized the four counties of Guangchang, Nanfeng, Xincheng, and Luxi; in the eighth month Shouqian's army was at Zhangjiaqiao in Fuzhou; three engagements were all victorious, but in hot pursuit they met an ambush and he died fighting.
translations.idiomatic: As rebels seized four counties, Shouqian won three battles at Zhangjiaqiao in August but was killed in an ambush during the pursuit.

sentences.zh: 時兆綸方赴鉛山，道梗，諮衢州鎮總兵饒廷選乞援。

translations.literal: At that time Zhaolun was on his way to Qianshan; the route was blocked; he consulted Brigadier-General Rao Tingxuan of Quzhou garrison and requested aid.
translations.idiomatic: En route to Qianshan with roads blocked, Zhaolun appealed to Brigadier Rao Tingxuan of Quzhou for help.

sentences.zh: 廷選率兵二千一百至，兆綸冒雨穿敵壘，復入廣信，共謀守禦，寇屢攻不下。

translations.literal: Tingxuan led twenty-one hundred troops to arrive; Zhaolun braved rain to pass through enemy fortifications and re-entered Guangxin; together they planned defense, and the bandits repeatedly attacked without taking it.
translations.idiomatic: Rao arrived with 2,100 men; Zhaolun cut through enemy lines in the rain to re-enter Guangxin, and together they held the city against repeated assaults.

sentences.zh: 凡七戰，捕斬其渠六，斬六千餘級。

translations.literal: In all seven battles they captured and beheaded six chieftains and beheaded more than six thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: In seven battles they killed six rebel leaders and more than six thousand men.

sentences.zh: 廷選與游擊穆隆阿、都司賴高翔等又屢擊破之。

translations.literal: Tingxuan together with brigade commander Mu Long'a, director Lai Gaoxiang, and others again repeatedly routed them.
translations.idiomatic: Rao Tingxuan, Mu Long'a, Lai Gaoxiang, and others repeatedly routed the rebels thereafter.

sentences.zh: 賊走玉山，廣信始解嚴。

translations.literal: The bandits fled to Yushan and Guangxin was at last relieved from emergency.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels withdrew toward Yushan and the emergency at Guangxin ended.

sentences.zh: 兆綸防守危城，盡出俸銀餉軍，貧困至不能自給，尋以病告歸。

translations.literal: Zhaolun defended the endangered city, paid out all his salary to supply the army, became so impoverished that he could not support himself, and shortly requested leave to return home on account of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Defending the besieged city, Zhaolun spent his entire salary on the troops until he could barely support himself, then retired on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 七年，病痊，仍直南書房，署工部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, when his illness had healed, he again served in the Southern Library and acted as vice minister of works.
translations.idiomatic: Recovered in 1857, he returned to the Southern Library and served as acting Vice Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 八年，授戶部侍郎，調倉場侍郎。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was appointed vice minister of revenue and transferred to vice minister in charge of the granary depot.
translations.idiomatic: In 1858 he became Vice Minister of Revenue and was transferred to the granary depot.

sentences.zh: 時軍事方急，兆綸疏請責成督撫辦賊，略曰：「今於督撫外另設統兵大員，其本省督撫雖有會剿之名，其實專為籌餉之事。

translations.literal: Military affairs were urgent at the time; Zhaolun memorialized requesting that governors-general and governors be held responsible for dealing with bandits, stating in summary: "Today, apart from governors-general and governors, separate overall military commanders are additionally established; although the provincial governors-general and governors of each province have the name of joint suppression, in fact they are devoted solely to provisioning affairs.
translations.idiomatic: With the war still urgent, Zhaolun argued that governors should be held responsible for suppressing rebels: "Separate supreme commanders now shadow provincial governors, who nominally join campaigns but in practice handle only supplies.

sentences.zh: 統兵者往往以呼應不靈，餉糈不給，漸至遷延；

translations.literal: The overall commanders often, because coordination is not responsive and provisions are not supplied, gradually come to delay;
translations.idiomatic: Supreme commanders delay when coordination fails and rations run short;

sentences.zh: 而督撫又往往以事權不一，供億不貲，各生意見。

translations.literal: while governors-general and governors likewise often, because authority is not unified and expenditures cannot be met, each form separate opinions.
translations.idiomatic: while governors withhold support because their authority is divided and costs are unsustainable.

sentences.zh: 及至城池失守，統兵者無地方之責，或邀寬大之恩，而並未帶兵之督撫，轉受其咎。

translations.literal: When cities and towns are lost, the overall commanders bear no local responsibility and may seek leniency, while governors-general and governors who did not even lead troops bear the blame instead.
translations.idiomatic: When cities fall, commanders without local responsibility may plead for leniency while governors who never led troops take the blame.

sentences.zh: 名實不符，事多掣肘，賊氛之熾，職此之由。

translations.literal: Names and realities do not match, affairs are much hindered; this is the reason the bandit atmosphere has flared.
translations.idiomatic: This mismatch of name and responsibility, he argued, was why rebel power kept growing.

sentences.zh: 臣惟督撫大吏，類皆朝廷簡拔之人，設其人未盡知兵，不妨擇統兵大員，畀以督撫之任，使之各清各省，而責其成功。

translations.literal: Your servant considers that governors-general and governors are mostly men selected and promoted by the court; if any among them do not fully know military affairs, there is no harm in choosing overall military commanders and entrusting them with the duties of governor-general or governor, so that each may pacify his province and be held responsible for success.
translations.idiomatic: Since governors are men the court chooses itself, he proposed giving proven commanders gubernatorial authority so each province could be cleared and its leaders held accountable.

sentences.zh: 方今川、黔、閩、廣，並未另派統兵大員，而本境漸就肅清。

translations.literal: At present in Sichuan, Guizhou, Fujian, and Guangdong, no separate overall military commanders have been additionally dispatched, yet those regions are gradually being pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Sichuan, Guizhou, Fujian, and Guangdong had no separate supreme commanders yet were gradually pacified.

sentences.zh: 湖南北之專任督撫討賊者，轉有餘力助剿鄰境。

translations.literal: In Hunan and northern Hubei, where governors-general and governors were solely charged with suppressing bandits, they in turn had surplus strength to assist in suppressing neighboring territories.
translations.idiomatic: Hunan and northern Hubei, where governors alone fought rebels, even had strength to aid neighboring provinces.

sentences.zh: 至於江蘇一省，統兵者不一而足，而潰敗糜爛至今。

translations.literal: As for Jiangsu province alone, overall commanders are more than one would wish, yet collapse and ruin continue to this day.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangsu, by contrast, had more than enough supreme commanders yet remained in ruins.

sentences.zh: 平心而論，統兵大員中，豈乏公忠體國之臣？

translations.literal: Speaking with calm fairness, among the overall commanders, are there not lacking loyal ministers who embody the public good and the state?
translations.idiomatic: Many supreme commanders were loyal and public-spirited, he conceded.

sentences.zh: 所以然者，抑其所處之地不同，用情亦異，此其故不可不深長思也。

translations.literal: The reason is rather that the places where they are situated differ and the dispositions with which they are employed also differ; this cause cannot but be deeply and carefully pondered.
translations.idiomatic: But their assignments and incentives differed—a point, he insisted, worth serious reflection.

sentences.zh: 清、淮一帶，實為南北要衝，漕運總督不兼管地方，宜此時權設江北巡撫，抑或將漕運總督權改斯缺，所有江北各路軍務，悉歸統制，庶可控扼江、淮，聲援汝、潁。

translations.literal: The Qing and Huai region is in truth the vital passage between north and south; the grain transport governor-general does not concurrently administer local territory; at this time one should provisionally establish a governor of Jiangbei, or alternatively convert the grain transport governor-general's authority to that post; all military affairs of the various routes of Jiangbei should be wholly placed under unified control, so that the Yangtze and Huai may be controlled and Run and Ying may be supported.
translations.idiomatic: The Qing-Huai corridor was the strategic hinge between north and south; he proposed a Jiangbei governor or expanded grain-transport authority to unify northern military command and secure the Yangtze-Huai and Run-Ying regions.

sentences.zh: 不惟江南群逆絕其覬覦之心，即豫東會、捻各匪出沒之區，亦可斷其一臂矣。」

translations.literal: Not only would the diverse rebels of Jiangnan be cut off in their covetous designs, but even in the regions where the Nian bandits of eastern Henan roam, one wing could also be severed."
translations.idiomatic: That would not only check Jiangnan rebels but also weaken the Nian bands roaming eastern Henan."

sentences.zh: 疏上，不報。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted but received no response.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was ignored.

sentences.zh: 九年，英吉利兵北犯，疏請以戰為和。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, when English troops invaded northward, he memorialized requesting that war be used to achieve peace.
translations.idiomatic: In 1859, as British forces marched north, he argued that only fighting could secure peace.

sentences.zh: 十年，英兵掠豐益倉，兆綸疏自劾，上寬之。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, when English troops plundered the Fengyi Granary, Zhaolun memorialized impeaching himself; the emperor was lenient with him.
translations.idiomatic: In 1860, after British troops looted the Fengyi Granary, Zhaolun submitted a self-impeachment that the emperor declined to accept.

sentences.zh: 又疏言：「軍興以來，各省兵不足，因招募鄉勇。

translations.literal: He again memorialized: "Since the rise of military mobilization, the troops of each province have been insufficient, and local braves have therefore been recruited.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote: "Since the war began, regular troops proved insufficient and provinces turned to militia.

sentences.zh: 比來兵日少，勇日增，不可不預為之計。

translations.literal: Recently troops grow daily fewer while braves grow daily more numerous; one cannot fail to plan for this in advance.
translations.idiomatic: Regular troops were shrinking while militia grew—a trend that needed planning.

sentences.zh: 此後勇丁如有技藝精嫺，戰陣得力者，請令統兵督撫大臣，即於存營缺額挑選充補。

translations.literal: Henceforth, if any brave soldiers have refined skill in arts and prove effective in battle array, I request that the overall military commanders and governors-general and governors be ordered immediately to select them from existing camp vacancies to fill gaps.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that skilled militiamen who proved themselves in battle be recruited into regular army vacancies.

sentences.zh: 軍事既定，原歸農者遣散，原效力者分隸各標，序補額兵。」

translations.literal: Once military affairs were settled, those who had originally returned to farming were dismissed, those who had originally served were assigned to various banners, and regular quota troops were filled in sequence."
translations.idiomatic: When peace returned, farmers went home, remaining fighters were assigned to regular units, and vacant army posts were filled in order."

sentences.zh: 上韙之。

translations.literal: The emperor praised it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 兆綸以交河糧商囤積穀秕，遣勇目捕治，糧商訴勇目索詐，辭連兆綸，事上聞，命刑部逮問。

translations.literal: Because Jiaohe grain merchants had hoarded inferior grain, Zhaolun sent a brave officer to arrest and punish them; the merchants accused the officer of extortion, implicating Zhaolun in their testimony; the matter reached the emperor, who ordered the Ministry of Punishments to arrest and investigate.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaolun sent a militia officer to punish Jiaohe grain merchants hoarding bad grain; they claimed extortion and implicated him, prompting an imperial order for the Ministry of Punishments to investigate.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，京察休致。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi, he retired through the metropolitan evaluation.
translations.idiomatic: In 1862 he retired after the metropolitan officials' review.

sentences.zh: 二年，諭責兆綸在任用人不當，奪職銜。

translations.literal: In the second year, an edict censured Zhaolun for improper use of personnel while in office and stripped his rank titles.
translations.idiomatic: In 1863 an edict censured him for poor appointments and stripped his honorary ranks.

sentences.zh: 兆綸感知遇，遇事敢言，以是多齟《齒吾》。

translations.literal: Zhaolun, sensing imperial favor, spoke boldly when matters arose, and for this reason often clashed with others.
translations.idiomatic: Grateful for imperial trust, he spoke out freely—and often found himself at odds with colleagues.

sentences.zh: 罷官歸，讓產諸弟，主問津書院，以修脯自給。

translations.literal: After leaving office he returned home, yielded his property to his younger brothers, headed the Wenjin Academy, and supported himself on teaching stipends.
translations.idiomatic: Back home after dismissal, he gave his estate to his brothers, ran the Wenjin Academy, and lived on lecture fees.

sentences.zh: 六年，卒。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 1867.

sentences.zh: =雷以諴=雷以諴，字鶴皋，湖北咸寧人。

translations.literal: Lei Yixian, courtesy name He Gao, was a native of Xianning in Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: Lei Yixian, whose courtesy name was He Gao, came from Xianning in Hubei Province.

sentences.zh: 道光三年進士，授刑部主事，洊升郎中。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the third year of Daoguang, was appointed a principal clerk in the Ministry of Punishments, and was repeatedly promoted to bureau director.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of 1823, he entered the Ministry of Punishments and rose to bureau director.

sentences.zh: 遷御史、給事中，擢內閣侍讀學士，三遷奉天府府丞。

translations.literal: He was transferred to censor and supervising secretary, promoted to reader-in-waiting of the Grand Secretariat, and thrice promoted to vice prefect of Shuntian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He served as censor and supervising secretary, became a reader-in-waiting of the Grand Secretariat, and after three promotions was vice prefect of Shuntian.

sentences.zh: 咸豐元年，應詔陳言，請任賢能，覈名實。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianfeng, responding to an imperial call for memorials, he asked that the talented be employed and names be checked against reality.
translations.idiomatic: In 1851 he memorialized urging appointment of the capable and verification of official merit.

sentences.zh: 二年，复授太常寺少卿，屢上疏陳軍事。

translations.literal: In the second year he was again appointed vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and repeatedly submitted memorials on military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In 1852 he returned as vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and often wrote on military matters.

sentences.zh: 三年，遷左副都御史，命會同河道總督楊以增巡視黃河口岸，迭疏請撫卹茌平、東平、東阿、汶上饑民，撤山東防河兵，省各渡口冗費，皆報可。

translations.literal: In the third year he was promoted to vice censor-in-chief; he was ordered to tour the Yellow River ports jointly with Governor-General of Rivers and Channels Yang Yizeng, and in successive memorials requested relief for famine victims in Chiping, Dongping, Dong'e, and Wenshang, withdrawal of Shandong river-defense troops, and reduction of redundant expenses at the various ferry crossings—all approved.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to vice censor-in-chief in 1853, he inspected Yellow River ports with Yang Yizeng, secured relief for famine counties, cut Shandong river-defense troops and ferry expenses—all approved.

sentences.zh: 粵匪陷揚州，以諴自請討賊，募勇屯萬福橋，扼揚州東南。

translations.literal: When Cantonese bandits captured Yangzhou, Yixian volunteered to attack the rebels, recruited braves to encamp at Wanfu Bridge, and blocked the southeast approach to Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After rebels took Yangzhou, Yixian volunteered to fight, raised militia at Wanfu Bridge, and held the city's southeast flank.

sentences.zh: 賊窺裡下河，以諴屢擊走之，通、泰十餘城賴以保全。

translations.literal: When the rebels probed the inner lower river region, Yixian repeatedly drove them off, and more than ten cities in Tong and Tai were thereby preserved.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly repelled rebel probes of the inner lower river area, saving more than ten cities in Tongzhou and Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 授刑部侍郎，幫辦軍務。

translations.literal: He was appointed vice minister of the Ministry of Punishments and assisted in managing military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was made vice minister of punishments and helped handle military affairs.

sentences.zh: 與琦善、陳金綬會攻揚州，以諴分兵駐守要隘，焚浦口賊舟。

translations.literal: Joining Qi Shan and Chen Jinshou in a joint attack on Yangzhou, Yixian divided his troops to garrison strategic passes and burned rebel boats at Pukou.
translations.idiomatic: With Qi Shan and Chen Jinshou he besieged Yangzhou, garrisoned key passes, and burned rebel boats at Pukou.

sentences.zh: 屢會諸軍擊賊，而揚州久攻不能下，諸將以總兵瞿騰龍最勇敢足恃，詔命援安徽。

translations.literal: Repeatedly joining the various armies to strike the rebels, yet Yangzhou could not be taken after a long siege; the generals considered brigade commander Qu Tenglong the bravest and most reliable, and an edict ordered him to reinforce Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: Repeated assaults failed to take Yangzhou; the generals trusted brigade commander Qu Tenglong most, and the court ordered him to Anhui.

sentences.zh: 以諴疏言：「臨陣易將，兵家所忌。」

translations.literal: Yixian memorialized: "Replacing a general on the eve of battle is what strategists forbid."
translations.idiomatic: Yixian wrote: "Replacing a commander in the middle of battle is a classic military mistake."

sentences.zh: 琦善亦以為言，乃留勿遣。

translations.literal: Qi Shan said the same, and Qu was therefore kept and not sent away.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Shan agreed, and Qu was kept from going.

sentences.zh: 其冬，賊陷儀徵，偪運河西岸，官軍屢擊走之。

translations.literal: That winter the rebels captured Yizheng, pressed the west bank of the Grand Canal, and were repeatedly driven off by government troops.
translations.idiomatic: That winter rebels took Yizheng and pressed the canal's west bank until driven back repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 以諴與浙閩總督慧成合駐軍灣頭六徬，未幾，賊援至，鄉勇潰散，琦善奏劾，奪官留軍自效。

translations.literal: Yixian and Zhejiang-Fujian Governor-General Huicheng jointly encamped at Wantou Liubang; before long rebel reinforcements arrived, local braves scattered in rout, Qi Shan memorialized to impeach him, his rank was stripped, and he was kept with the army to redeem himself.
translations.idiomatic: Yixian and Governor-General Huicheng camped at Wantou Liubang; when reinforcements routed the militia, Qi Shan impeached him, stripped his rank, and kept him in the field to redeem himself.

sentences.zh: 嗣琦善請移灣頭大營，以諴與慧成力爭，琦善复劾以諴諱飾。

translations.literal: Later Qi Shan requested moving the main camp from Wantou; Yixian and Huicheng strenuously objected, and Qi Shan again impeached Yixian for concealing and glossing over facts.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi Shan wanted to move the main camp, Yixian and Huicheng objected fiercely; Qi Shan impeached Yixian again for covering up failures.

sentences.zh: 上責琦善諉過，飭以諴仍守灣頭及萬福橋諸隘。

translations.literal: The emperor rebuked Qi Shan for shifting blame and ordered Yixian still to defend Wantou and the passes at Wanfu Bridge and elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rebuked Qi Shan for blame-shifting and ordered Yixian to keep defending Wantou and Wanfu Bridge.

sentences.zh: 賊既自揚州退瓜洲，時來攻，以諴與陳金綬合擊敗之，加三品頂戴。

translations.literal: After the rebels withdrew from Yangzhou to Guazhou and came from time to time to attack, Yixian and Chen Jinshou jointly struck and defeated them, and he was given a third-rank top button.
translations.idiomatic: When rebels retreating to Guazhou raided repeatedly, he and Chen Jinshou defeated them and he received a third-rank top button.

sentences.zh: 尋授江蘇布政使，屢督砲船渡江會剿，攻北固山，破其土城，乘勝逐至金山，敗之。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Jiangsu financial commissioner; he repeatedly directed gunboats across the river in joint suppression, attacked Beigu Mountain, broke its earthen wall, pursued in victory to Jinshan, and defeated the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Soon made Jiangsu financial commissioner, he led gunboats across the river, took Beigu Mountain's earthen wall, pursued to Jinshan, and won.

sentences.zh: 六年，托明阿兵潰瓜洲，揚州复陷，詔責以諴等擁兵不援。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, when Tuoming'a's troops were routed at Guazhou and Yangzhou again fell, an edict censured Yixian and others for holding troops without coming to the rescue.
translations.idiomatic: In 1856, after Tuoming'a's rout at Guazhou and Yangzhou's fall, an edict blamed Yixian for failing to reinforce.

sentences.zh: 又疏辨冒功，為德興阿所劾，褫職戍新疆。

translations.literal: He again memorialized to rebut charges of falsely claiming merit, was impeached by Dexing'a, stripped of office, and banished to garrison duty in Xinjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Defending himself against charges of false credit, he was impeached by Dexing'a, dismissed, and sent to Xinjiang.

sentences.zh: 以諴在戍所，呈請將軍扎拉芬代奏，言江北軍事。

translations.literal: While in exile, Yixian submitted a petition through General Zhalafen to memorialize on military affairs north of the Yangtze.
translations.idiomatic: From exile he had General Zhalafen relay memorials on Jiangbei military affairs.

sentences.zh: 尋赦還，賜四品頂戴，授陝西按察使。

translations.literal: Soon he was pardoned and recalled, granted a fourth-rank top button, and appointed Shaanxi surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Soon pardoned, he received a fourth-rank top button and became Shaanxi surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 遷布政使，入為光祿寺卿。

translations.literal: He was transferred to financial commissioner and entered the capital as director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: He became financial commissioner and then director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments in the capital.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，京察，休致。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi, at the metropolitan evaluation, he retired.
translations.idiomatic: In 1862 he retired after the metropolitan review.

sentences.zh: 光緒五年，以重宴鹿鳴還原銜。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Guangxu, because of a second banquet for juren of his year, his original rank titles were restored.
translations.idiomatic: In 1879 a second Deer Cry banquet for his cohort restored his original ranks.

sentences.zh: 八年，又以重宴恩榮，加頭品頂戴。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, because of another banquet of imperial grace and honor, he was given a first-rank top button.
translations.idiomatic: In 1882 another grace banquet earned him a first-rank top button.

sentences.zh: 十年，卒，年七十九。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, he died at the age of seventy-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 1884, aged seventy-nine.

sentences.zh: 以諴在江北，用幕客錢江策，創收釐捐。

translations.literal: While Yixian was in Jiangbei, he adopted a plan from his staff member Qian Jiang and pioneered the collection of likin levies.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiangbei, Yixian adopted staff member Qian Jiang's plan and pioneered the likin tax.

sentences.zh: 錢江者，浙江長興諸生，嘗以策幹揚威將軍奕經，不能用。

translations.literal: Qian Jiang was a licentiate of Changxing in Zhejiang; he had once presented a plan to General Yijing, the Displaying Majesty general, but was not employed.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Jiang, a Changxing licentiate, had once offered strategy to General Yijing without success.

sentences.zh: 林則徐戍伊犁，從之出關，以是知名。

translations.literal: When Lin Zexu was banished to Ili, Jiang followed him out through the pass and thereby became well known.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Lin Zexu into exile at Ili and gained renown.

sentences.zh: 謁以諴於邵伯，留佐幕，餉絀，江獻策，遣官吏分駐水陸要衝，設局卡，行商經過，視貨值高下定稅率，千取其一，名曰「釐捐」，亦並徵坐賈，歲得錢數千萬緡。

translations.literal: He visited Yixian at Shaobo, stayed on as a staff assistant; when supplies ran short, Jiang offered a plan—officials were dispatched to garrison key points by land and water, collection bureaus and checkpoints were set up, and passing merchants were taxed at a rate fixed according to the value of goods, one part in a thousand, named "likin"; stationary merchants were taxed as well, yielding tens of millions of cash strings each year.
translations.idiomatic: At Shaobo he joined Yixian's staff; when funds ran out he proposed likin—checkpoints on land and water taxed merchants one-thousandth of goods' value, plus stationary shops, yielding tens of millions of strings of cash yearly.

sentences.zh: 江與同幕五人赴下河督勸，不從者脅以兵，民間目為「五虎」。

translations.literal: Jiang and five fellow staff members went to the lower river region to supervise and urge compliance; those who would not comply were coerced by troops, and the people called them the "Five Tigers."
translations.idiomatic: Jiang and five staffmates enforced collection in the lower river area, threatening recalcitrants with troops; locals called them the "Five Tigers."

sentences.zh: 江自以為功，累保獎至道員，氣矜益盛，以諴不能堪。

translations.literal: Jiang took the credit for himself, was repeatedly recommended and rewarded up to circuit intendant, grew ever more arrogant, and Yixian could not endure it.
translations.idiomatic: He took full credit, rose by recommendation to circuit intendant, and grew insufferably arrogant—more than Yixian could bear.

sentences.zh: 會飲，江使酒罵坐，以諴執而殺之，以跋扈狂肆、謀不軌聞。

translations.literal: At a drinking gathering Jiang, drunk, cursed those present; Yixian had him seized and killed, sparking reports of overbearing arrogance, wild license, and treasonous design.
translations.idiomatic: At a banquet the drunk Jiang abused the company; Yixian had him seized and killed, amid reports of arrogance and sedition.

sentences.zh: 後各省皆仿其例以濟軍需，為歲入大宗焉。

translations.literal: Later every province followed this example to meet military needs, and it became a major source of annual revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Later provinces copied the model to fund armies, making likin a major revenue source.

sentences.zh: =陶樑=陶樑，字鳧薌，江蘇長洲人。

translations.literal: Tao Liang, courtesy name Fuxiang, was a native of Changzhou in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Liang, whose courtesy name was Fuxiang, came from Changzhou in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶十三年進士，選庶吉士，授編修，纂修皇清文穎。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the thirteenth year of Jiaqing, was selected a bachelor of the Hanlin Academy, appointed compiler, and helped compile the Imperial Qing Literary Exemplars.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of 1808, he entered the Hanlin, became a compiler, and worked on the Imperial Qing Literary Exemplars.

sentences.zh: 十九年，林清之變，逆黨闌入禁城，樑方在館修書，其僕駱升聞警，匿樑於書櫥，自當戶立，賊刃之，僕，越日事定，樑出，救之甦。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year, at the Lin Qing incident, rebel partisans broke into the Forbidden City; Liang was in the Hanlin hall compiling books when his servant Luo Sheng heard the alarm, hid Liang in a bookcase, himself stood blocking the door, and was cut down by the rebels; the next day, when affairs were settled, Liang emerged and revived him.
translations.idiomatic: During the 1813 Lin Qing raid, his servant Luo Sheng hid him in a bookcase, stood guard at the door, and was stabbed; Liang revived him after the attack.

sentences.zh: 仁宗回鑾聞之，召樑問狀，曰：「義僕也！」

translations.literal: When the Jiaqing Emperor returned to the capital and heard of it, he summoned Liang to ask what had happened and said: "A faithful servant!"
translations.idiomatic: On returning to the capital the Jiaqing Emperor summoned Liang and said: "A loyal servant!

sentences.zh: 賜之金。

translations.literal: He rewarded him with gold.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rewarded him with gold.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，以知府發直隸，補永平，調正定。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he was dispatched to Zhili as prefect, appointed to Yongping, and transferred to Zhengding.
translations.idiomatic: In 1816 he went to Zhili as prefect, serving Yongping and then Zhengding.

sentences.zh: 道光四年，擢清河道，署按察使。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Daoguang he was promoted to director of the Qinghe Route and acted as surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In 1824 he became director of the Qinghe Route and acting surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 新城縣失過境餉鞘，歸罪外委白勤，逮訊，死於刑。

translations.literal: When Xincheng County lost a convoy of transported pay passing through its territory, blame was fixed on the sub-official Bai Qin; he was arrested and interrogated and died under torture.
translations.idiomatic: After Xincheng lost a silver convoy, sub-official Bai Qin was blamed, arrested, and died under interrogation.

sentences.zh: 上遣尚書松筠、侍郎白鎔按治，察其枉，樑坐降四級，捐复知府，留直隸。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Minister Songyun and Vice Minister Bai Rong to investigate; finding Bai Qin had been wronged, Liang was demoted four ranks, bought back his prefecture, and remained in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: Songyun and Bai Rong found Bai Qin innocent; Liang was demoted four ranks, bought back his prefect post, and stayed in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 十二年，補大名知府。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was appointed prefect of Daming.
translations.idiomatic: In 1832 he became prefect of Daming.

sentences.zh: 十八年，遷湖北荊宜施道，萬城堤決，樑复坐降調，捐复。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he was transferred to the Jing-Yi-Shi circuit in Hubei; when the Wancheng dike burst, Liang again suffered demotion and transfer, then bought back his rank.
