translations.idiomatic: In 1838 he took the Jing-Yi-Shi circuit in Hubei; the Wancheng dike breach cost him another demotion, which he bought back.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，補湖南糧儲道，調湖北漢黃德道。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he was appointed grain storage intendant of Hunan and transferred to the Han-Huang-De circuit in Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: In 1842 he became Hunan grain intendant, then Hubei's Han-Huang-De intendant.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，遷甘肅按察使，調山西。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year he was promoted to Gansu surveillance commissioner and transferred to Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In 1848 he became Gansu surveillance commissioner, then moved to Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，遷江西布政使。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year he was promoted to Jiangxi financial commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In 1849 he became Jiangxi financial commissioner.

sentences.zh: 入覲，授太常寺卿。

translations.literal: On entering court for audience, he was appointed director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: After an audience he became director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 文宗即位，樑疏言：「宣宗成皇帝天錫智勇，嘉慶十九年八月之變，當時但傳發槍斃賊，不知首逆林清姓名地址，亦由宮中訊得，立時遣捕，故渠魁不致遠颺，餘孽不致滋蔓。

translations.literal: When the Xianfeng Emperor ascended the throne, Liang memorialized: "The late Daoguang Emperor was heaven-endowed with wisdom and courage; at the August incident of the nineteenth year of Jiaqing, at the time it was only reported that guns were fired and rebels killed, without knowing the name and address of the chief traitor Lin Qing—they too were obtained through palace interrogation and troops were immediately dispatched to arrest him, so the ringleader did not flee far and the remnants did not spread.
translations.idiomatic: At Xianfeng's accession Liang wrote: "Heaven gave the Daoguang Emperor wisdom and courage; in the 1813 crisis only gunfire was reported until palace interrogation revealed Lin Qing's identity and troops captured him before the rebellion spread.

sentences.zh: 請敕載入實錄，以揚聖武。」

translations.literal: I request an edict that this be entered in the Veritable Records to proclaim imperial martial prowess."
translations.idiomatic: He asked that this be recorded in the Veritable Records to honor imperial martial virtue."

sentences.zh: 上從之。

translations.literal: The emperor agreed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor assented.

sentences.zh: 咸豐二年，擢內閣學士。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianfeng he was promoted to secretary of the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In 1852 he became a Grand Secretariat secretary.

sentences.zh: 四年，遷禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was transferred to vice minister of the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In 1854 he became vice minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 六年，以病乞罷。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, citing illness, he requested retirement.
translations.idiomatic: In 1856 ill health prompted his retirement request.

sentences.zh: 七年，卒，年八十六。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he died at the age of eighty-six.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 1857, aged eighty-six.

sentences.zh: 樑早有文名，曾從侍郎王昶助其纂述。

translations.literal: Liang had early won literary fame and once assisted Vice Minister Wang Chang in his compilations.
translations.idiomatic: He was known early for letters and once assisted Wang Chang's editorial work.

sentences.zh: 歷官所至，提倡風雅，賓接才俊，輯畿輔詩傳行世。

translations.literal: Wherever he served he promoted elegant letters, received talented men as guests, and compiled the Poetry of the Capital Region for circulation.
translations.idiomatic: In every post he fostered literary culture, patronized talent, and published a collection of metropolitan poetry.

sentences.zh: 晚登朝右，時值軍興，耆舊凋落，其猶見乾、嘉文物之盛者，惟大學士祁藻與樑二人，為士林所歸仰雲。

translations.literal: Late in life he rose to high court rank; at a time of military mobilization the old worthies were dying off, and of those who still bore witness to the cultural splendor of the Qianlong and Jiaqing reigns, only Grand Secretary Qi Zao and Liang remained—the two whom the scholar-official world looked up to.
translations.idiomatic: Late in a career that reached the highest ranks, as war thinned the older generation, he and Grand Secretary Qi Zao were the last witnesses to Qianlong-Jiaqing culture whom scholars revered.

sentences.zh: =吳存義=吳存義，字和甫，江蘇泰興人。

translations.literal: Wu Cunyi, courtesy name Hefu, was a native of Taixing in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Cunyi, whose courtesy name was Hefu, came from Taixing in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 道光十八年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the eighteenth year of Daoguang, was selected a bachelor of the Hanlin Academy, and appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of 1838, he entered the Hanlin as a compiler.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，督雲南學政。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he supervised education in Yunnan as provincial education commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In 1842 he became Yunnan's education commissioner.

sentences.zh: 邊徼士風敦樸，存義力為提倡，文風改觀。

translations.literal: Scholarly customs on the frontier were simple and solid; Cunyi exerted himself to promote them, and literary culture was transformed.
translations.idiomatic: On the frontier he vigorously promoted plain, solid scholarship and changed local literary culture.

sentences.zh: 回民煽亂，存義按試永昌竟，出郭數里，城中火起，待學使去而始發也。

translations.literal: When Hui people stirred rebellion, Cunyi had just finished examinations in Yongchang; he went several li outside the city walls, fires rose in the city—it had waited until the education commissioner left before breaking out.
translations.idiomatic: During a Hui uprising he finished exams at Yongchang and left the city; fires broke out only after the commissioner had gone several li beyond the walls.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，丁母憂歸。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year he returned home upon the death of his mother.
translations.idiomatic: In 1848 he went home to mourn his mother.

sentences.zh: 會江北大水洊飢，存義議賑，躬詣富室勸捐，多感其誠，出貲購米穀。

translations.literal: Just then repeated floods in Jiangbei brought famine; Cunyi proposed relief, personally visited wealthy households to urge donations, and many, moved by his sincerity, contributed funds to buy rice and grain.
translations.idiomatic: During Jiangbei flood famine he organized relief, personally soliciting wealthy donors who responded with grain and rice.

sentences.zh: 存義棹小舟散給饑民，全活甚眾。

translations.literal: Cunyi poled a small boat to distribute supplies to the starving, saving a great many lives.
translations.idiomatic: He poled a small boat distributing food and saved many lives.

sentences.zh: 服闋，直南書房，擢侍講。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he served in the Southern Studio and was promoted to expositor.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning he joined the Southern Studio and became an expositor.

sentences.zh: 咸豐五年，典試雲南，复留督學政，士益親之。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Xianfeng he presided over the Yunnan examinations, was again retained as education commissioner, and the scholars grew still closer to him.
translations.idiomatic: In 1855 he examined Yunnan again, stayed on as education commissioner, and won still greater affection from scholars.

sentences.zh: 回亂益棘，圍會城，城中兵閧，掠官署民居，獨未入學政廨，民間婦孺匿考院避難者千人。

translations.literal: The Hui rebellion grew more severe and besieged the provincial capital; soldiers in the city mutinied and looted government offices and private homes, yet they did not enter the education commissioner's yamen; a thousand women and children from among the people hid in the examination hall to escape trouble.
translations.idiomatic: As the Hui crisis worsened and besieged the capital, mutinous troops looted the city but spared the education office; a thousand civilians sheltered in the exam hall.

sentences.zh: 存義在雲南久，習知民情，比復命奏對，陳變亂始末甚詳。

translations.literal: Cunyi had long been in Yunnan and was thoroughly familiar with local sentiment; when he returned to report and answered at audience, he set forth the beginning and end of the upheaval in great detail.
translations.idiomatic: Long familiar with Yunnan, he gave the throne a detailed account of the rebellion when he reported back.

sentences.zh: 累遷侍讀學士，署順天府丞。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to reader-in-waiting and acted as vice prefect of Shuntian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to reader-in-waiting and acted as vice prefect of Shuntian.

sentences.zh: 十年，英法聯軍入京師，上幸熱河，京朝官多挈家出走，存義屬疾，語家人毋隨人妄動。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, when the Anglo-French allied armies entered the capital and the emperor fled to Rehe, many metropolitan officials fled with their families; Cunyi claimed illness and told his household not to follow others in rash movement.
translations.idiomatic: In 1860 when allied forces entered Beijing and the court fled to Rehe, he feigned illness and told his family not to join the exodus.

sentences.zh: 事定，敘城守勞，將入存義名，存義聞之，力疾起，署牘曰：「府丞吳存義抱病家居，幹掫詰姦皆無與。

translations.literal: When affairs were settled, meritorious service in defending the city was registered and Cunyi's name was to be entered; hearing this, Cunyi forced himself up despite illness and signed a document stating: "Vice Prefect Wu Cunyi, ill at home, had no part in patrol or interrogation of wrongdoers.
translations.idiomatic: When rewards for city defense were listed, he forced himself up and signed a statement: "Vice Prefect Wu Cunyi lay ill at home and took no part in patrol or arrest duties.

sentences.zh: 今病未癒，不敢冒受賞。」

translations.literal: My illness is not yet cured; I dare not receive reward improperly."
translations.idiomatic: I am still ill and dare not accept reward I do not deserve."

sentences.zh: 未幾，擢太僕寺卿，遷通政使，署禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: Before long he was promoted to director of the Court of Imperial Stud, transferred to commissioner of the Office of Transmission, and acted as vice minister of the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he became director of the Court of Imperial Stud, transmission commissioner, and acting vice minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 存義以文廟從祀位次多舛，奏請審定，繪圖頒行。

translations.literal: Cunyi, finding the order of enshrined worthies in Confucian temples often wrong, memorialized requesting a definitive arrangement and had charts drawn and issued.
translations.idiomatic: Finding Confucian temple enshrinement orders wrong, he had them audited and published in charts.

sentences.zh: 又以諸儒增祀既繁，漸失世用其書、垂諸國冑之義，奏飭中外臣工不得濫請。

translations.literal: He also held that since enshrined Confucians had grown too numerous, the meaning of putting their books to use in the world and handing them down to the imperial heirs was gradually lost, and memorialized ordering officials inside and outside not to make requests indiscriminately.
translations.idiomatic: He also argued that proliferating enshrinements betrayed the purpose of honoring scholars whose books served the state and instructed officials to stop indiscriminate requests.

sentences.zh: 署刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: He acted as vice minister of the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He served as acting vice minister of punishments.

sentences.zh: 同治二年，署工部侍郎，迭署禮、戶二部。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tongzhi he acted as vice minister of the Ministry of Works and in succession acted in the Ministries of Rites and Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In 1863 he acted as vice minister of works and successively of rites and revenue.

sentences.zh: 出督浙江學政，軍事甫定，人士離散初歸，存義寬大拊循，歲考既週，秀良者始奮於學，乃導以經、史、小學，文風復興。

translations.literal: Sent out to supervise education in Zhejiang, with military affairs just settled and scholars scattered and only beginning to return, Cunyi treated them generously and comfortingly; once the annual examinations had run a full cycle, able students began to revive in study, and he then guided them in the classics, history, and evidential philology, and literary culture revived.
translations.idiomatic: As Zhejiang education commissioner after the war, he gently rebuilt schools; after a year of exams able students returned to classical, historical, and philological study.

sentences.zh: 三年，調吏部，留學政任。

translations.literal: In the third year he was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel but was retained in his education commissionership.
translations.idiomatic: In 1864 he moved to the Ministry of Personnel but kept his education post.

sentences.zh: 六年，任滿，以病乞歸。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, when his term was complete, he requested return home citing illness.
translations.idiomatic: In 1867 his term ended and illness prompted his retirement.

sentences.zh: 七年，卒。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 1868.

sentences.zh: =殷兆鏞=殷兆鏞，字譜經，江蘇吳江人。

translations.literal: Yin Zhaoyong, courtesy name Pujing, was a native of Wujiang in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Zhaoyong, whose courtesy name was Pujing, came from Wujiang in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 道光二十年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the twentieth year of Daoguang, was selected a bachelor of the Hanlin Academy, and appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of 1840, he entered the Hanlin as a compiler.

sentences.zh: 咸豐四年，遷侍講，直上書房，授惠親王子奕詳等讀。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Xianfeng he was promoted to expositor, entered the Upper Study, and instructed Prince Yi's son Yixin and others in reading.
translations.idiomatic: In 1854 he became expositor in the Upper Study, tutoring Prince Yi's son Yixin and others.

sentences.zh: 擢侍講學士，命授孚郡王奕硉讀，累遷大理寺少卿。

translations.literal: He was promoted to expositor-in-waiting, ordered to instruct Prince Fu Yi Lu in reading, and was repeatedly promoted to vice director of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to expositor-in-waiting, he tutored Prince Fu Yi Lu and rose to vice director of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 八年，英吉利兵犯天津，兆鏞力主戰，疏請黜邪謀，決不計，詆斥主和諸臣甚力，擢詹事。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, when English troops attacked Tianjin, Zhaoyong forcefully advocated war, memorialized requesting dismissal of evil counsel and resolute action regardless of cost, fiercely denounced the peace-minded ministers, and was promoted to court tutor.
translations.idiomatic: In 1858 when British forces threatened Tianjin, he argued fiercely for war, denounced peace advocates, and was promoted to court tutor.

sentences.zh: 九年，署兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, he served as acting vice minister of the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: In 1859 he served as acting vice minister of war.

sentences.zh: 詔江蘇諸省治團練，兆鏞疏言其弊，舉四害，言甚切。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the Jiangsu provinces to organize local militia training; Zhaoyong memorialized on its abuses, citing four harms, and spoke very sharply.
translations.idiomatic: When the court ordered Jiangsu to organize militia training, Zhaoyong memorialized against it, listing four harms in sharp terms.

sentences.zh: 上海欲借英、法人助戰，兆鏞亦以為不可。

translations.literal: Shanghai wished to borrow English and French troops to assist in fighting; Zhaoyong also held this impossible.
translations.idiomatic: Shanghai proposed enlisting British and French troops; Zhaoyong opposed that too.

sentences.zh: 十一年，丁本生母憂，同治元年，服除，仍直上書房。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he observed mourning for his birth mother; in the first year of Tongzhi, when mourning ended, he again entered the Upper Study.
translations.idiomatic: In 1861 he mourned his birth mother; when mourning ended in 1862 he returned to the Upper Study.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「江、皖軍威既震，大局漸有轉機。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "The military prestige of Jiangsu and Anhui has already been established, and the overall situation is gradually turning.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote: "With Jiangsu and Anhui armies regaining their edge, the larger struggle is slowly turning.

sentences.zh: 臣來自災區，敢就見聞真切關係重大者為皇上陳之：一，宜飭戎行。

translations.literal: Your subject comes from the disaster zone and dares, on the basis of what he has seen and heard that is truly reliable and of great importance, to lay before Your Majesty: first, the army should be admonished.
translations.idiomatic: Having come from the stricken region, I venture to report what I have seen that matters most: first, the army must be brought to order.

sentences.zh: 上海兵勇號稱四萬，皆不堪用，何以今年經英、法人管帶，便成勁旅？

translations.literal: Shanghai's soldiers and braves are said to number forty thousand, all unusable—why is it that this year, once placed under English and French command, they became crack troops?
translations.idiomatic: Shanghai claims forty thousand troops, yet none fight well—how did British and French officers this year turn them into a crack force?

sentences.zh: 華爾親兵六百，盡中國人，戰無不勝。

translations.literal: Ward's personal troops numbered six hundred, all Chinese, and they won every battle fought.
translations.idiomatic: Ward's six hundred personal guards were all Chinese and won every battle.

sentences.zh: 無他，挑選慎，約束嚴，器械精，賞罰信耳。

translations.literal: There is nothing else to it: careful selection, strict discipline, fine weapons, and trustworthy rewards and punishments, that is all.
translations.idiomatic: Nothing else—strict selection, tight discipline, good arms, and reliable reward and punishment.

sentences.zh: 請敕將帥講求武備，漸事安攘。

translations.literal: I ask that generals and commanders be ordered to study military readiness and gradually carry out pacification.
translations.idiomatic: Order commanders to train properly and pacify the region step by step.

sentences.zh: 提鎮中如曾秉忠水師通賊焚掠；

translations.literal: Among regional commanders, Zeng Bingzhong's naval forces colluded with bandits in burning and plunder;
translations.idiomatic: Among brigade and regional commanders, Zeng Bingzhong's fleet colludes with rebels in looting;

sentences.zh: 馬德昭掠蘇州、上海；

translations.literal: Ma Dezhao plundered Suzhou and Shanghai;
translations.idiomatic: Ma Dezhao raids Suzhou and Shanghai;

sentences.zh: 李定泰掠湖州、嘉興；

translations.literal: Li Dingtai plundered Huzhou and Jiaxing;
translations.idiomatic: Li Dingtai raids Huzhou and Jiaxing;

sentences.zh: 向奎每戰輒敗，敗輒行劫；

translations.literal: Xiang Kui was defeated in every battle, and after each defeat he turned to robbery;
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Kui loses every battle and loots after each defeat;

sentences.zh: 馮日坤部兵掠婦女。

translations.literal: Feng Rikun's troops plundered women.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Rikun's men abduct women.

sentences.zh: 李恆嵩兵不行劫，已共推良將。

translations.literal: Li Hengsong's troops did not engage in robbery, and he was already jointly acclaimed as a good general.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hengsong's troops do not loot, and all hail him as a capable commander.

sentences.zh: 竊謂行師首禁焚掠，克城先謀戍守，否則旋得旋失，民間無孑遺矣。

translations.literal: I privately hold that on campaign the first prohibition must be burning and plunder; when cities are taken, garrison defense must be planned first—otherwise gains are lost as soon as made, and among the people none will be left alive.
translations.idiomatic: Campaigns must forbid looting first; taking a city means garrisoning it—or gains slip away at once and civilians are wiped out.

sentences.zh: 一，宜澄吏治。

translations.literal: Second, official administration should be clarified.
translations.idiomatic: Second, clean up local governance.

sentences.zh: 上海諸官吏，惟劉郇膏得民心，已蒙特簡。

translations.literal: Among Shanghai's officials, only Liu Genggao won the people's hearts and had already received special imperial appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Of Shanghai officials, only Liu Genggao enjoys popular trust and has already received imperial appointment.

sentences.zh: 薛煥統馭無能；

translations.literal: Xue Huan was incompetent in overall command;
translations.idiomatic: Xue Huan commands fecklessly;

sentences.zh: 吳煦精心計，在上海設銀號，繳捐者非所出銀票不收；

translations.literal: Wu Xu was crafty in scheming, established a bank in Shanghai, and would accept no donation unless paid in notes issued by him;
translations.idiomatic: Wu Xu schemes craftily, runs a bank in Shanghai, and accepts donations only in his own notes;

sentences.zh: 新授糧儲道楊坊，由洋行擔水夫致巨富，為洋人所鄙；

translations.literal: The newly appointed grain commissioner Yang Fang rose from water-carrier for foreign firms to great wealth and was despised by foreigners;
translations.idiomatic: Yang Fang, newly made grain commissioner, grew rich from carrying water for foreign firms and is despised even by foreigners;

sentences.zh: 浙江布政使林福祥，杭州破後降賊，送王有齡、張錫庚柩至上海。

translations.literal: Zhejiang provincial treasurer Lin Fuxiang surrendered to bandits after Hangzhou fell and sent the coffins of Wang Youling and Zhang Xigeng to Shanghai.
translations.idiomatic: Zhejiang treasurer Lin Fuxiang surrendered after Hangzhou fell and sent Wang Youling's and Zhang Xigeng's coffins to Shanghai.

sentences.zh: 臣意此等悖員，宜分別懲創，稍申憲典。

translations.literal: Your subject's view is that such perverse officials should be separately punished and corrected, so as somewhat to uphold the penal code.
translations.idiomatic: Such wayward officials should be punished by degree to uphold the law.

sentences.zh: 一，宜清釐餉款。

translations.literal: Third, military pay and funds should be audited and clarified.
translations.idiomatic: Third, audit military funds.

sentences.zh: 上海左近官卡、賊卡、槍船卡林立，卡稅之外，釐捐、月捐、船捐、畝捐、房捐日增月益，臣聞官吏紳商皆云日可收銀二萬，月得六十萬。

translations.literal: Near Shanghai official checkpoints, bandit checkpoints, and armed-boat checkpoints stand in dense array; beyond checkpoint duties, lijin, monthly levies, boat levies, land levies, and house levies increase day by day and month by month—I hear officials, gentry, and merchants all say twenty thousand taels can be collected daily, six hundred thousand monthly.
translations.idiomatic: Checkpoints—official, rebel, and gunboat—crowd Shanghai's approaches; on top of tolls, lijin and levies on boats, land, and houses grow monthly. Officials and merchants say receipts reach twenty thousand taels a day, six hundred thousand a month.

sentences.zh: 兵勇四萬人，日餉三錢，月止三十六萬，而當局猶入不敷出。

translations.literal: Forty thousand soldiers and braves at three cash daily pay need only three hundred sixty thousand monthly, yet the authorities still fall short of income.
translations.idiomatic: Forty thousand troops at three cash a day need only three hundred sixty thousand taels monthly—yet authorities still run deficits.

sentences.zh: 請敕曾國籓、李鴻章嚴密清釐。

translations.literal: I ask that Zeng Guofan and Li Hongzhang be ordered to conduct a strict audit.
translations.idiomatic: Order Zeng Guofan and Li Hongzhang to audit accounts strictly.

sentences.zh: 蘇、松、嘉、湖賦額甲天下，近三十年，年年蠲緩，官民交欠，賦成虛額。

translations.literal: Suzhou, Songjiang, Jiaxing, and Huzhou had land-tax quotas foremost in the empire; for nearly thirty years remissions and deferrals were granted every year, officials and people mutually in arrears, and the tax yield became a paper figure.
translations.idiomatic: Suzhou, Songjiang, Jiaxing, and Huzhou once led the empire in land tax, but thirty years of remissions left officials and people in mutual arrears and quotas hollow.

sentences.zh: 現經大亂，田荒戶絕，可否俟軍務大定，敕督撫覈計，酌留商稅，核減農賦，以羨補不足，勿逾定則。

translations.literal: Now after great disorder, fields lie waste and households are extinguished—might it be possible, once military affairs are settled, to order governors-general and governors to reckon accounts, retain commercial taxes as appropriate, reduce agricultural levies, use surpluses to cover shortfalls, and not exceed fixed rules?
translations.idiomatic: After such devastation, could governors wait until order returns, then trim farm levies, keep commercial taxes, cover gaps from surpluses, and stay within fixed quotas?

sentences.zh: 一，宜撫卹遺民。

translations.literal: Fourth, surviving people should be comforted and relieved.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth, succor the survivors.

sentences.zh: 江、浙交界莠民設槍船，所至焚掠，此輩視官兵盛衰以為向背，克復時必為內應。

translations.literal: Wicked men on the Jiangsu-Zhejiang border operate armed boats and burn and plunder wherever they go; this sort gauge whether official troops are strong or weak to decide which way to turn, and on recovery will surely serve as inside collaborators.
translations.idiomatic: Ruffians on the Jiangsu-Zhejiang border run gunboats and loot wherever they sail; they will switch sides with military fortunes and aid rebels when cities fall.

sentences.zh: 請敕督撫從宜處置，或令歸農，或籍為兵，勿貽後患。

translations.literal: I ask that governors-general and governors dispose of them as circumstances require—either order them back to farming or enroll them as soldiers—and leave no trouble for later.
translations.idiomatic: Let governors resettle them as farmers or enroll them as soldiers before they become a lasting threat.

sentences.zh: 至失守郡縣，陷賊士民商賈，苟非出自甘心，僅止偷生畏死，可否援脅從罔治之義，乞恩原宥。

translations.literal: As for lost prefectures and counties, gentry, commoners, and merchants who fell among bandits—if they did not act from willing hearts but only sought to live and feared death—might the principle that coercion excuses punishment be invoked to beg grace and pardon?
translations.idiomatic: For civilians and merchants trapped in fallen counties who obeyed rebels only to survive, invoke the rule that coercion excuses guilt and grant mercy.

sentences.zh: 一，宜防維外人。

translations.literal: Fifth, foreigners should be guarded against and managed.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth, guard against foreign influence.

sentences.zh: 上海孤城克保，不得謂非外人之力。

translations.literal: That the isolated city of Shanghai was saved cannot be said to be without foreign power.
translations.idiomatic: Shanghai's survival owes much to foreigners.

sentences.zh: 自經助剿，所向無前，或云實出義舉，或云欲通商販，或云日後恃功索償，臣俱不敢逆億。

translations.literal: Since they began assisting in suppression, they advanced everywhere without opposition—some say it was truly righteous action, some say they wished to trade, some say they will later claim merit and demand repayment—I dare not guess against any of these.
translations.idiomatic: Since they joined the fight they have swept all before them—some call it charity, some trade, some a future bill for services—I dare not presume which.

sentences.zh: 各處通商，尊奉外人太過。

translations.literal: At every treaty port foreigners are honored and served excessively.
translations.idiomatic: Every treaty port defers to foreigners too readily.

sentences.zh: 猶幸我國新政清明，未萌覬覦。

translations.literal: Fortunately our country's new policies are clear and bright, and covetous designs have not yet sprouted.
translations.idiomatic: Fortunate still that clear governance has not yet stirred their covetousness.

sentences.zh: 日久相習，利權盡歸，人情益附，而謂狼子必無野心，實難深信。

translations.literal: As days lengthen and habits form, profit and power pass entirely to them, human sentiment attaches ever more—yet to say a wolf's cub must have no wild ambition is truly hard to believe deeply.
translations.idiomatic: Over time profit and loyalty shift their way; to believe the wolf's cub lacks ambition is hard indeed.

sentences.zh: 撫禦得體，尤在博知外情。

translations.literal: To comfort and control appropriately depends above all on broadly knowing foreign conditions.
translations.idiomatic: Proper handling depends above all on understanding foreign conditions.

sentences.zh: 請敕各口通商衙門，譯述各國新聞有關時事者，書記大則奏聞，藉資豫備。」

translations.literal: I ask that each treaty-port trade office be ordered to translate and relay foreign news bearing on current affairs; matters of great import should be memorialized to the throne, to aid foresight and preparation."
translations.idiomatic: Order treaty ports to translate foreign news on current affairs and report weighty items to the throne for preparedness."

sentences.zh: 上以所陳不為無見，下國籓、鴻章等籌畫，並將福祥等察劾按治。

translations.literal: The emperor held that what was set forth was not without insight, issued orders to Guofan, Hongzhang, and others to plan, and also ordered investigation and punishment of Fuxiang and the rest.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor found merit in the memorial, ordered Guofan and Hongzhang to act, and directed investigation of Fuxiang and others.

sentences.zh: 尋授詹事，遷內閣學士，迭署兵、禮諸部侍郎。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed court tutor, transferred to secretary of the Grand Secretariat, and successively served as acting vice minister of war, rites, and other ministries.
translations.idiomatic: He soon became court tutor and Grand Secretariat secretary, acting in turn as vice minister of war and rites.

sentences.zh: 四年，編修蔡壽祺疏劾恭親王，命大學士倭仁等察奏。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, compiler Cai Shouqi memorialized impeaching Prince Gong; the emperor ordered Grand Secretaries Woren and others to investigate and report.
translations.idiomatic: In 1865 compiler Cai Shouqi impeached Prince Gong; the emperor ordered Woren and others to investigate.

sentences.zh: 兆鏞與左都御史潘祖廕疏言：「恭親王輔政以來，功過久蒙睿照，重臣進退，關係安危。

translations.literal: Zhaoyong and left censor-in-chief Pan Zuyin memorialized: "Since Prince Gong assisted in government, his merits and faults have long enjoyed the emperor's discerning regard; the advancement and removal of great ministers concerns safety and peril.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaoyong and Pan Zuyin wrote: "Prince Gong's record under regency has long enjoyed imperial scrutiny; dismissing a great minister touches the dynasty's safety.

sentences.zh: 尚祈持平用中，熟思審處，察其悔過，予以轉圜。

translations.literal: I still pray for balanced, centrist use, mature thought and careful disposition, observation of his repentance, and granting him a way to turn the situation around.
translations.idiomatic: We pray Your Majesty will weigh the matter evenly, consider carefully, note his repentance, and give him room to make amends.

sentences.zh: 庶無紊黜陟大綱，滋天下後世之惑。」

translations.literal: Thus the great pattern of dismissal and promotion will not be disordered, nor confusion bred for the world and posterity."
translations.idiomatic: So the principles of appointment will not be unsettled nor future ages left bewildered."

sentences.zh: 上納其言。

translations.literal: The emperor accepted their words.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took their advice.

sentences.zh: 六年，督安徽學政。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he supervised education in Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: In 1867 he became Anhui education commissioner.

sentences.zh: 七年，授禮部侍郎，任滿，仍直上書房，迭署兵、工二部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was appointed vice minister of rites; when his term ended he again entered the Upper Study and successively served as acting vice minister of war and works.
translations.idiomatic: In 1868 he became vice minister of rites; when his term ended he returned to the Upper Study and acted as vice minister of war and works in turn.

sentences.zh: 尋授吏部侍郎，調戶部，再調禮部。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed vice minister of personnel, transferred to revenue, and again transferred to rites.
translations.idiomatic: He soon became vice minister of personnel, then revenue, then rites again.

sentences.zh: 光緒七年，以病乞罷。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Guangxu, citing illness, he requested retirement.
translations.idiomatic: In 1881 ill health prompted his retirement.

sentences.zh: 九年，卒。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 1883.

sentences.zh: =【論】=論曰：咸豐中四方多故，文宗悒悒，恆抱疾。

translations.literal: Commentary says: In the Xianfeng era troubles arose on all sides; the Wenzong Emperor was downcast and constantly ill.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: Under Xianfeng troubles rose everywhere; Emperor Wenzong was melancholy and often ill.

sentences.zh: 京師用不足，大錢鈔票，法立弊滋。

translations.literal: The capital lacked funds; large-coin notes were issued—as soon as the law was established, abuses multiplied.
translations.idiomatic: Capital funds ran short; large coins and paper notes bred new abuses as soon as they were introduced.

sentences.zh: 王茂廕屢進讜言，均中利害，清直為一時之最，宋晉亦其次也。

translations.literal: Wang Maoyin repeatedly submitted forthright counsel, all hitting profit and harm; in integrity and uprightness he was foremost of his age, and Song Jin ranked next.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Maoyin's blunt memorials always hit the mark; none was more upright in his day, with Song Jin close behind.

sentences.zh: 袁希祖、文瑞皆有所論列，而徐繼畬直箴君德，所舉三防，陳義尤高，發桂言軍事亦有識。

translations.literal: Yuan Xizu and Wen Rui both offered remonstrances; Xu Jiyu directly admonished imperial virtue—his three warnings he raised were especially lofty in principle—and Fa Gui spoke on military affairs with discernment as well.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Xizu and Wen Rui also remonstrated; Xu Jiyu admonished imperial conduct with lofty "three guard" principles, and Fa Gui showed sound judgment on military affairs.

sentences.zh: 廉兆綸助守江西，雷以諴分防江北，並著事功。

translations.literal: Lian Zhaolun helped defend Jiangxi and Lei Yixian held the northern Jiang defenses—both achieved notable service.
translations.idiomatic: Lian Zhaolun aided Jiangxi's defense and Lei Yixian guarded northern Jiangsu; both won distinction.

sentences.zh: 陶樑為文學老宿，吳存義、殷兆鏞並侍從清望，存義視學滇、浙，能得士心，兆鏞慷慨論事，於鄉邦疾苦冀有補苴，何言之深也！

translations.literal: Tao Liang was a veteran of letters; Wu Cunyì and Yin Zhaoyong both enjoyed repute as palace attendants—Cunyì supervised education in Yunnan and Zhejiang and could win scholars' hearts; Zhaoyong argued affairs with generous passion, hoping to patch the sufferings of his home region—how deeply he spoke!
translations.idiomatic: Tao Liang was a literary elder; Wu Cunyì and Yin Zhaoyong both held standing at court—Cunyì won scholars' hearts inspecting Yunnan and Zhejiang; Zhaoyong spoke boldly on public affairs, hoping to relieve his homeland's woes—what depth of feeling!
